nodes.label: Monitoring and Alert Response Activity Flow
nodes.rationale: UML activity diagram for the poultry monitoring system: a single linear operational loop from data capture through risk evaluation, alerting, actuation, human acknowledgement and outcome logging. The diagram deliberately closes the loop with a logging step so every alert produces an auditable record.
nodes.norm_label: monitoring and alert response activity flow

nodes.label: Capture Sensor & Vision Data
nodes.rationale: Sensor telemetry and computer-vision inference are fused at the same entry activity rather than as two separate pipelines, so risk evaluation always sees both modalities for the same time window.

nodes.label: Risk Detected? (decision node)
nodes.rationale: Branch node with a 'no' edge looping back to capture and a 'yes' edge into alert generation, so the system idles cheaply in the common no-risk case.

nodes.label: Trigger Fan/Heater
nodes.rationale: Automated actuation fires immediately after alert generation and before human notification, so environmental correction is not blocked on operator response latency.

nodes.label: Resolve & Log Outcome
nodes.rationale: Terminal activity persists the outcome so alert history becomes farm record data, supporting later analysis rather than being discarded once the alert clears.

nodes.label: Alert Lifecycle State Machine
nodes.rationale: UML state machine with five states (NORMAL, WARNING, CRITICAL, ACKNOWLEDGED, RESOLVED). Escalation and de-escalation are modelled explicitly so an alert can worsen or improve without being recreated, preserving a single alert identity across its whole life.

nodes.label: WARNING Alert State
nodes.rationale: Entered on threshold breach; exits either back to NORMAL when the condition clears with hysteresis, upward to CRITICAL when it worsens, or sideways to ACKNOWLEDGED on operator action.

nodes.label: ACKNOWLEDGED Alert State
nodes.rationale: Acknowledgement is a distinct state rather than a boolean flag, so the system can distinguish 'a human has seen this' from 'the physical condition is fixed'.

nodes.label: Hysteresis Threshold Clearing
nodes.rationale: The WARNING to NORMAL transition is explicitly annotated 'clears (hysteresis)': the clear threshold is offset from the trip threshold so a sensor value oscillating around the limit does not produce a storm of alert/clear events. This is the diagram's main anti-flapping design decision.

nodes.label: Farm Management Domain Class Model
nodes.rationale: UML class diagram of the persistence model: User/Farm/Pen/Batch form the ownership spine, with Device attached per pen and all record types (mortality, feed, health, sensor, vision, alert) hanging off it as 1..* or 0..* time-series children.

nodes.label: User (username, role, email, is_active)
nodes.rationale: Carries an explicit role attribute rather than relying on group membership, indicating role-based access control is modelled directly in the domain.

nodes.label: Batch (code, breed, start_date, initial_qty)
nodes.rationale: Batch rather than Pen owns the husbandry records, so history follows the flock cohort across its production cycle instead of being tied to physical housing.

nodes.label: Device (uuid, token, pen, last_seen)
nodes.rationale: Holds its own uuid and token, so each edge node authenticates independently to the REST API; last_seen supports liveness/heartbeat detection without a separate table.

nodes.label: SensorReading (ts, temp, humidity, gas, level)
nodes.rationale: A single wide row per timestamp rather than one row per metric, trading normalisation for cheap time-aligned reads on the dashboard.

nodes.label: VisionResult (ts, class, confidence)
nodes.rationale: Stores only class label and confidence per timestamp, not bounding boxes or frames, so the server keeps inference summaries while raw imagery stays at the edge.

nodes.label: Alert (ts, type, severity, status)
nodes.rationale: The status attribute is the persisted projection of the alert state machine; severity is kept separate from status so escalation and lifecycle progress are independent axes.

nodes.label: System Component Architecture
nodes.rationale: Three-tier component view: an edge tier (sensing, Python runtime, inference, SQLite buffer, REST client), a server tier (Django REST API, farm management core, ORM layer, PostgreSQL) and a presentation tier (Bootstrap web UI). The REST boundary is the only coupling between edge and server.

nodes.label: Edge Runtime (Python service)
nodes.rationale: A single Python service orchestrates sensing, inference, buffering and upload, keeping the edge deployable as one process on constrained hardware.

nodes.label: Inference Engine (TFLite/ONNX)
nodes.rationale: TFLite/ONNX rather than full TensorFlow or PyTorch at the edge: quantised runtimes fit the Raspberry Pi footprint and let the model be swapped without changing the host service.

nodes.label: Local Buffer (SQLite)
nodes.rationale: An on-device SQLite store absorbs readings while connectivity is down, making the edge tolerant of intermittent rural networks; data is drained to the server by the REST client when the link returns.

nodes.label: Django REST API
nodes.rationale: Serves as the single ingress for both device telemetry and the web UI, so authentication and validation are implemented once.

nodes.label: Web UI (Bootstrap)
nodes.rationale: Server-rendered Bootstrap rather than an SPA framework, minimising client-side build tooling and keeping the dashboard usable on low-end phones.

nodes.label: Deployment Topology
nodes.rationale: UML deployment diagram with two execution sites: the poultry house edge site (Raspberry Pi device plus sensors and relays) and a VPS/on-prem server node hosting Nginx, Gunicorn+Django and PostgreSQL containers, reached over HTTPS REST. A browser node represents operator access.

nodes.label: Raspberry Pi 4/5 (device node)
nodes.rationale: Commodity single-board computer chosen as the edge host: cheap enough to replicate per poultry house and powerful enough to run quantised vision inference locally.

nodes.label: Server (VPS / on-prem)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately specified as 'VPS / on-prem' so the same containerised stack can be hosted in the cloud or inside the farm, avoiding a hard dependency on external connectivity.

nodes.label: HTTPS REST Communication Path
nodes.rationale: Both the edge device and the operator browser reach the server over HTTPS only; there is no inbound path to the poultry house, so the edge site needs no port forwarding or static address.

nodes.label: PyTorch 1.12.1 / Torchvision 0.13.1 Runtime Stack
nodes.rationale: Despite the directory name advertising a TF/Keras YOLOv4, the declared runtime is torch/torchvision plus opencv-python, rich and tqdm - the vendored tree actually executes on PyTorch.

nodes.label: Norfair Tracking Library Dependency
nodes.rationale: Pulled directly from git master (git+https://github.com/tryolabs/norfair.git@master) rather than a released version, so tracking behaviour is not reproducible across installs - an unpinned VCS dependency in an otherwise fully pinned file.

nodes.label: Exact Version Pinning Policy
nodes.rationale: Every PyPI dependency uses == exact pins (torch==1.12.1, numpy==1.21.6, opencv-python==4.6.0.66) to freeze the CUDA/NumPy ABI combination that the detector was validated against; the single git dependency escapes this policy.

nodes.rationale: Three-class blood cell detection vocabulary shipped with the upstream YOLOv4 repository as a custom-dataset example; unrelated to poultry behaviour and retained only as vendored sample data.

nodes.rationale: Ordered 80-label vocabulary whose index order is load-bearing: detector class ids map positionally into this file, so reordering silently mislabels every detection. Contains 'bird' but no chicken-specific class, which is why the project needs a retrained head for poultry.

nodes.label: Pretrained Weight Download Procedure
nodes.rationale: Weights are fetched by shell scripts at setup time rather than committed to the repository, keeping the checkout small; the procedure assumes a POSIX shell (sudo chmod +x, ./get_*.sh), so it does not run as written on Windows.

nodes.label: YOLOv3 Pretrained Weights (get_yolo.sh)
nodes.rationale: Downloaded into examples/pretrained_models/yolo_weights - note this path is under examples/, unlike the SSD models which live at the repository-root pretrained_models/, an inconsistency in the documented layout.

nodes.label: Caffemodel MobileNetSSD Weights (get_caffemodel.sh)
nodes.rationale: Third interchangeable detector backend; offering YOLOv3, TF-SSD and Caffe-SSD side by side shows the tracker is designed to be detector-agnostic.

nodes.label: Multi-Object Tracker Dependency Set
nodes.rationale: Fully unpinned (numpy, scipy, matplotlib, opencv-contrib-python, pandas, motmetrics, setuptools, ipyfilechooser) - the opposite policy to the sibling yolo-v4-tf.keras requirements file, so the two vendored trees cannot be guaranteed to co-install cleanly. opencv-contrib-python here versus opencv-python there is a direct conflict: the two packages cannot both be installed.

nodes.label: motmetrics Evaluation Dependency
nodes.rationale: py-motmetrics is what makes the MOTA/MOTP evaluation harness possible; its presence in the runtime requirements (rather than a dev-extras file) means evaluation is treated as a first-class capability of the tracker package.

nodes.label: Multi-Object Tracker Examples Index
nodes.rationale: Splits the examples into three tiers - notebooks for exploration, scripts for reproducible runs, and motmetrics evaluations for measurement - and links out to GitHub rather than to local paths.

nodes.label: Model Weights Prerequisite for Examples
nodes.rationale: The readme opens with an explicit note that network models must be downloaded before any example will run, pointing at ../DOWNLOAD_WEIGHTS.md - the examples are intentionally shipped without weights to keep the repository lightweight, at the cost of a mandatory manual setup step.

nodes.label: Example Script --help CLI Convention
nodes.rationale: Instead of documenting each script's flags in prose, the readme defers entirely to 'python3 <file-name.py> --help', making the argparse definitions the single source of truth and preventing documentation drift.

nodes.label: MOT Challenge File Format
nodes.rationale: Ten-column CSV schema <frame>, <id>, <bb_left>, <bb_top>, <bb_width>, <bb_height>, <conf>, <x>, <y>, <z>. Tracker output is required to use the identical schema as ground truth so a single parser and a single comparison routine serve both sides of the evaluation.

nodes.label: MOTChallenge IO Round-Trip Fixture
nodes.rationale: Five-line minimal fixture (frames 1-2, ids 1-4) exercising the MOTChallenge reader: integer boxes, conf=1 and the -1,-1,-1 world-coordinate sentinel that marks 2D-only data.

nodes.label: VATIC Annotation IO Fixture
nodes.rationale: Space-delimited VATIC format with lost/occluded/generated flags, a quoted class label ('worker', 'pc') and a variable-length trailing attribute list - a fundamentally different shape from MOTChallenge CSV, which is why the reader needs a separate parser rather than a delimiter switch.

nodes.label: TUD-Campus Ground Truth Annotations
nodes.rationale: 359 hand-annotated pedestrian instances with integer bounding boxes and conf=1 on every row - the conf column is used as a validity flag in ground truth rather than as a detector score.

nodes.label: TUD-Campus Tracker Output
nodes.rationale: 222 rows against 359 ground-truth rows, with fractional box coordinates and conf=-1: the tracker under-reports detections and emits sub-pixel estimates, which is exactly the miss/precision gap MOTA is meant to quantify. Track ids jump (3, 6, 10) because ids are allocated globally, not per surviving track.

nodes.label: TUD-Stadtmitte Ground Truth Annotations
nodes.rationale: 1156 rows and, unlike TUD-Campus, populated world x/y coordinates (e.g. 4.4852, 5.5016) with z=0 - this sequence carries calibrated ground-plane positions, enabling 3D-distance matching instead of IoU.

nodes.label: TUD-Stadtmitte Tracker Output
nodes.rationale: 749 rows with fractional boxes and all world coordinates set to -1, so even though the ground truth supplies 3D positions the tracker output cannot be matched in world space - evaluation must fall back to 2D IoU.

nodes.label: TUD-Stadtmitte Tracker Output (root multi-object-tracker copy)
nodes.rationale: Byte-identical 749-row duplicate of the copy nested under yolo-v4-tf.keras/. The project vendors multi-object-tracker twice - once at the repository root and once inside the YOLOv4 tree - so evaluation fixtures exist in two places and can drift independently.

nodes.label: Example Video Datasets (cars, cows, people)
nodes.rationale: Sample footage is referenced as external Flickr links (cars, cows, people) rather than committed, avoiding both repository bloat and redistribution of third-party video; the cost is that examples break if the links rot.

nodes.label: Example Video Datasets (root multi-object-tracker copy)
nodes.rationale: Identical duplicate of the video_data readme in the nested yolo-v4-tf.keras copy of the tracker, confirming the whole examples/ tree is vendored twice.

nodes.label: Layered Request Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Requests traverse routing, middleware, view, permission, validation and ORM layers in a fixed order so that authentication, CSRF and role enforcement always execute before any data touches the database; templates and JSON responses share the same view layer to avoid duplicating business logic between the HTML dashboard and the REST API consumed by the Raspberry Pi.

nodes.label: Hysteresis and Minimum On/Off Time
nodes.rationale: Banded thresholds plus a minimum on/off dwell time stop the fan and heater relays from chattering when a reading oscillates around a setpoint; this protects relay and mains-switched equipment lifetime and avoids alert storms from transient sensor noise.

nodes.label: Farm-Pen-Batch Ownership Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: All operational records hang off either BATCH (husbandry events) or DEVICE (machine-generated telemetry), and both roll up through PEN to FARM to USER. This single ownership chain lets every row be scoped to a farm for role-based access control with one join path instead of per-table permission logic.

nodes.label: Analogue-to-Digital Conversion Requirement
nodes.rationale: The Raspberry Pi has no on-board analogue input, so the MQ135's analogue gas signal must pass through an external MCP3008/ADS1115 ADC over SPI/I2C, whereas the DHT22 speaks a 1-wire digital protocol directly on GPIO.

nodes.label: Feedback / Refinement Loop
nodes.rationale: Each increment is re-evaluated against explicit acceptance criteria and fed back into planning rather than proceeding linearly, so hardware, ML and web subsystems can be de-risked separately and only integrated once their own exit criterion is met.

nodes.label: Edge Compute Budget Management
nodes.rationale: Frame skipping, quantised weights and multi-frame aggregation keep inference within the Raspberry Pi's CPU budget while suppressing single-frame false positives; low-confidence detections are dropped rather than transmitted, and flagged classes are queued for human verification so the model never triggers action autonomously.

nodes.label: Frame-Leakage-Free Splitting
nodes.rationale: Because much of the dataset is extracted from continuous video, neighbouring frames are near-duplicates; splitting at the clip rather than frame level prevents the same scene appearing in both train and test and inflating reported mAP. Transfer learning is used because the locally collected GreenFarms set is too small to train from scratch.

nodes.label: Server-Side Risk Rule Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Risk rules are evaluated on the server after the vision result is persisted rather than on the Pi, so thresholds can be retuned centrally without reflashing edge devices and every alert is backed by a stored, auditable prediction record.

nodes.label: Layered Separation of Concerns
nodes.rationale: Splitting perception, edge, communication, application and user concerns lets the Pi keep controlling ventilation during network outages while the Django tier owns long-term storage, reporting and role-based access; the only coupling between tiers is a token-authenticated HTTPS REST contract.

nodes.label: Token-Authenticated REST Contract
nodes.rationale: A small fixed set of endpoints (auth, readings, vision, heartbeat, config, alerts) forms the whole device-to-server contract. Token auth rather than session cookies suits a headless device, heartbeat gives liveness independent of data volume, and GET /api/config lets thresholds be pushed to the edge without a firmware update.

nodes.label: Edge Data-Quality Gate
nodes.rationale: Validation, median filtering and NaN handling run on the Pi before anything is queued, so noisy MQ135 warm-up drift and dropped DHT22 reads never reach the database or trigger spurious alerts; failed plausibility checks retry the read rather than propagating a bad value.

nodes.label: UUID-Idempotent Insert
nodes.rationale: Readings carry a client-generated UUID so a retry after a lost acknowledgement is de-duplicated server-side ('201 / duplicate ignored') instead of double-counting. The buffer only marks a row synced once the 201 arrives, giving at-least-once delivery with exactly-once storage over an unreliable rural link.

nodes.label: Offline-First Operation
nodes.rationale: Control actuation happens before transmission and readings are buffered in local SQLite, so ventilation and heating keep working through connectivity loss and backlogged records are POSTed on reconnect rather than being discarded.

nodes.label: Edge Runtime as Single Integration Point
nodes.rationale: The Pi edge runtime is the only component both the IoT and ML subsystems talk to, and the only one that speaks REST/HTTPS to the web subsystem; config and acknowledgements flow back down the same channel. This keeps the three subsystems independently testable and gives a single place to enforce authentication and buffering.

nodes.label: Dual-Principal Authentication
nodes.rationale: Human users and headless edge devices are modelled as separate actors reaching the same Authenticate use case, which then «include»s a single Validate Credentials / Token step — one verification path covers both username/password logins and device tokens.

nodes.label: Centrally Managed Alert Thresholds
nodes.rationale: Warning and critical bands are administrator-configurable server-side data rather than edge constants, which is what allows GET /api/config to push retuned thresholds to Raspberry Pi devices without reflashing them.

nodes.label: Farm Owner (Actor)
nodes.rationale: Top-level tenant/ownership actor. Owns farms and consumes cross-farm reporting; does not perform day-to-day operational data entry, which is delegated to Farm Manager and Farm Worker.

nodes.label: Manage Farms (UC04)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: Farm is the root aggregate of the tenancy hierarchy (Farm -> Pen -> Batch), so only the Farm Owner may create or modify it.

nodes.label: Authenticate (Shared Included Use Case)
nodes.rationale: Factored out as a single «include» target reused by every use case in the system rather than duplicated per flow; this makes authentication a non-optional cross-cutting precondition and keeps each use case diagram focused on its own business logic.

nodes.label: Farm Manager (Actor)
nodes.rationale: Operational supervisor role: holds the widest use case surface (structure, health, finance, alerts, reporting) sitting between the Farm Owner's ownership scope and the Farm Worker's data-entry scope.

nodes.label: Manage Pens (UC05)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: Pen is the physical housing unit carrying a capacity attribute; managing it is delegated to the Farm Manager because pen layout is an operational rather than ownership concern.

nodes.label: Manage Batches (UC06)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: Batch (flock cohort) is the central traceability unit that health, feeding, mortality and sales records all attach to.

nodes.label: Validate Pen Capacity
nodes.rationale: Modelled as a mandatory «include» rather than an optional «extend» so that overstocking is structurally impossible: no batch can be placed without the capacity guard running, enforcing welfare and stocking-density rules at the point of write.

nodes.label: Farm Worker (Actor)
nodes.rationale: Lowest-privilege human actor confined to daily observational data capture (chick entry, mortality, feeding, health observation) plus read-only dashboard access; cannot alter farm structure, inventory or finance.

nodes.label: Record Chick Entry (UC07)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: Establishes the opening flock quantity for a batch. Shared between Farm Worker and Farm Manager because chick placement may happen on either shift.

nodes.label: Record Mortality (UC08)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: Mortality is the primary welfare and profitability KPI; capture is pushed to the Farm Worker so it happens at the pen rather than being back-filled by management.

nodes.label: Update Flock Quantity
nodes.rationale: Included (not extended) so the live bird count is atomically decremented with the mortality record; this prevents drift between the mortality ledger and the current flock size, which downstream feed-conversion and stocking-density calculations depend on.

nodes.label: Record Feeding (UC09)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: Feed is the largest cost line, so consumption is captured as an operational event rather than inferred from purchase records.

nodes.label: Decrement Feed Inventory
nodes.rationale: Coupling feeding to an automatic stock decrement makes inventory self-maintaining: the store balance is a derived consequence of recorded operations instead of a separately keyed number that can silently diverge.

nodes.label: Veterinary Consultant (Actor)
nodes.rationale: External specialist actor granted a narrow health-domain slice (observations, treatment, vaccination, environmental charts, AI prediction review) without any financial, structural or inventory access — least-privilege applied to a third party.

nodes.label: Record Health Observation (UC10)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: Deliberately opened to both Farm Worker and Veterinary Consultant so symptom capture is not bottlenecked on the vet's presence; the worker records what is seen and the vet adds clinical interpretation to the same record.

nodes.label: Record Treatment (UC11)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: Restricted to Farm Manager and Veterinary Consultant (unlike observation, which the Farm Worker may perform) because administering medication carries withdrawal-period and residue-compliance consequences.

nodes.label: Record Vaccination (UC12)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: Kept as a separate use case from Record Treatment despite an identical actor set and structure, because vaccination is a scheduled prophylactic programme with its own calendar and audit trail rather than a reactive clinical intervention.

nodes.label: Manage Inventory (UC13)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: Manual stock adjustment is reserved for the Farm Manager while automatic decrements flow from worker-level operations, separating deliberate stock corrections from routine consumption.

nodes.label: Enforce Balance Rule
nodes.rationale: A mandatory invariant guard preventing negative or inconsistent stock balances; modelled as «include» so the rule cannot be bypassed by any inventory path.

nodes.label: Record Expense (UC14)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: The simplest financial flow: no additional «include» beyond authentication because an expense entry has no cross-entity invariant to enforce, unlike Record Sale which must bind to a batch.

nodes.label: Record Sale (UC15)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: Revenue side of the ledger, restricted to the Farm Manager and forced to reference a batch so profitability can be computed per cohort.

nodes.label: Link to Batch
nodes.rationale: Mandatory batch association is what makes end-to-end traceability and per-batch cost/revenue attribution possible; an unlinked sale would break the batch as the unit of financial analysis.

nodes.label: View Dashboard (UC16)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: The only use case shared by all three human farm roles (Owner, Manager, Worker) — read-only situational awareness is universal while write privileges are role-differentiated.

nodes.label: View Environmental Charts (UC17)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: Time-series visualisation of IoT sensor telemetry, scoped to Farm Manager and Veterinary Consultant because interpreting temperature/humidity trends against flock health is a diagnostic rather than a data-entry activity.

nodes.label: Review AI Prediction (UC18)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: The human-in-the-loop checkpoint for machine inference: AI output is advisory, never auto-actioned, and must be adjudicated by a Farm Manager or Veterinary Consultant before it affects flock management.

nodes.label: Confirm / Dismiss Flag
nodes.rationale: Binary adjudication step included in every review, producing the ground-truth labels that both audit the model's precision and provide a feedback corpus for retraining.

nodes.label: Acknowledge Alert (UC19)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: Separated from resolution so the alert lifecycle records two distinct timestamps — time-to-acknowledge (responsiveness) and time-to-resolve (effectiveness) — and so an alert cannot be silently closed without first being seen.

nodes.label: Resolve Alert (UC20)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: Composed of three mandatory includes (Authenticate, Log Corrective Action, Acknowledge Alert), making resolution a strictly ordered terminal state: an alert can only be closed by an authenticated manager who has acknowledged it and documented what was actually done.

nodes.label: Log Corrective Action
nodes.rationale: Forces accountability: closing an alert requires a written intervention record, converting the alert log into an auditable remediation history rather than a dismissible notification queue.

nodes.label: Generate Report (UC21)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: Available to Farm Owner and Farm Manager but not Farm Worker, mirroring the split between aggregate performance analysis and operational data capture.

nodes.label: Export (PDF/CSV)
nodes.rationale: Modelled as «extend» rather than «include» — the only optional behaviour among the report/alert flows — because viewing a report on screen is the base scenario and file export is a conditional add-on for offline sharing or accounting hand-off.

nodes.label: System Administrator (Actor)
nodes.rationale: Platform-level actor kept entirely outside the farm business domain; its sole use case is device fleet administration, so infrastructure privilege never implies access to farm operational or financial data.

nodes.label: Manage Edge Devices (UC22)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: Registration and lifecycle control of IoT hardware; centralising it under one administrator actor keeps the device trust boundary auditable.

nodes.label: Issue Device Token
nodes.rationale: Machine identity is provisioned per device rather than sharing a global API key, so a compromised sensor node can be revoked individually without disrupting the rest of the fleet; this is the credential that the Edge Device later presents to Authenticate.

nodes.label: Edge Device (Actor)
nodes.rationale: A non-human system actor treated as a first-class authenticating principal: it must pass the same «include» Authenticate gate as every human role, so telemetry ingestion is never an unauthenticated back door.

nodes.label: Submit Sensor Reading (UC23)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: Numeric environmental telemetry ingestion (temperature, humidity, ammonia, etc.) — the data source behind the environmental charts and threshold alerting.

nodes.label: Raise Alert
nodes.rationale: Modelled as «extend» on both ingestion paths because alerting is conditional on a threshold or anomaly being breached; the normal ingestion path must stay fast and unconditional, with alert generation firing only on the exceptional branch.

nodes.label: Submit Vision Result (UC24)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: Computer-vision inference is executed on the edge device and only the derived result is submitted, avoiding raw video upload — a bandwidth and privacy driven edge-first architecture choice that mirrors the sensor ingestion path exactly.

nodes.label: Send Heartbeat / Get Config (UC25)
nodes.source_location: UML use case diagram, single page
nodes.rationale: Combines liveness reporting and configuration pull into one round trip so the device polls outbound only — no inbound connection to farm hardware is required, which suits NAT'd/intermittent rural connectivity and lets thresholds be retuned centrally.

nodes.label: Generic Object List Scaffold
nodes.rationale: Six list templates across farms and feeding (breed, customer, pen, supplier, feedtype, feedusage) are byte-identical: they derive the page heading from request.resolver_match.url_name with cut:'_list'|title, iterate the ListView-supplied object_list, render a generic Record/Created two-column table, and include partials/_pagination.html. The design intent is that a plain Django ListView needs no bespoke template - copying one neutral scaffold per model keeps template_name resolution conventional (app/model_list.html) while avoiding writing bespoke markup for low-value reference tables. The trade-off is duplicated files that must all be edited together, and a generic column set that cannot show model-specific fields.

nodes.label: Generic CRUD Form Scaffold
nodes.rationale: farms/simple_form.html, farms/farm_form.html, farms/pen_form.html, feeding/record_form.html, finance/record_form.html and flocks/batch_form.html are identical: an Edit/Add title toggled on the presence of `object`, an `object_label` context variable for the human noun, csrf token, delegation of all field rendering to partials/_form_fields.html, multipart encoding always on, and history.back() for both Back and Cancel. One scaffold therefore serves every CreateView/UpdateView in the project. history.back() is chosen over a computed success/cancel URL so the template needs no per-model URL knowledge; the cost is that Cancel is browser-history dependent and breaks on a direct deep link. enctype=multipart/form-data is unconditional so file fields work without per-form configuration.

nodes.label: Role-Gated Action Visibility
nodes.rationale: Create/Edit buttons are wrapped in inline template conditions over user.is_superuser and user.role membership. Farm-level mutation is limited to ADMIN/OWNER, while batch-level mutation additionally admits MANAGER - operational flock work is delegated one rung further down than estate configuration. This is presentation-layer hiding only and duplicates the role string list in every template, so it must be backed by view-level permission checks to be a real control.

nodes.label: UID-Based Detail Routing
nodes.rationale: Every cross-entity link in the UI is built with {% url 'app:name' obj.uid %} rather than a primary key - farms:farm_detail, farms:pen_detail, flocks:batch_detail, flocks:batch_update, finance:sale_detail, finance:sale_update. Using an opaque uid keeps sequential database ids out of URLs, avoiding record-count leakage and enumeration of other tenants' farms, at the cost of a non-indexable lookup column unless uid is explicitly indexed.

nodes.label: Empty-State / Error-State UI Pattern
nodes.rationale: A single `.empty-state` block - Bootstrap icon, short heading, muted sentence, optional recovery action - serves both the HTTP error pages and the {% empty %} branch of every list table. Reusing one visual idiom means a zero-row table and a server fault read as the same class of 'nothing to show here' event, so users learn one recovery affordance. The error partial is parameterised by code/head/msg and injected into both auth_content and content blocks so it renders correctly whether or not the visitor is authenticated.

nodes.label: Server-Side GET Filtering and Search
nodes.rationale: Filtering is done with plain GET forms whose current state is re-read from request.GET (q, status, category) so the filtered view is bookmarkable and back-button safe. Select controls auto-submit via onchange=this.form.submit() to remove a click, which means the pattern degrades badly without JavaScript and fires a full page load per selection - accepted because the deployment target is low-spec browsers where server-rendered pages are cheaper than a client-side filter layer.

nodes.label: Flock Health KPI Row
nodes.rationale: Batch health is summarised as four stat tiles reusing dashboard/_stat.html: total_entries (placed), current_quantity, total_mortality and cumulative_mortality_rate. Placed vs current vs mortality is the closing identity of a broiler batch, so the row doubles as a data-integrity check, and cumulative mortality rate is the primary welfare/performance alarm metric surfaced ahead of the detailed mortality and weight logs beneath it.

nodes.label: Generic Paginated Record List Scaffold
nodes.rationale: A single copy-pasted list template body (search form on GET 'q', table over object_list rendering str(obj) plus created_at, an empty-state block, and an included pagination partial) is reused verbatim across flocks, health, inventory and iot apps. The trade-off is deliberate: it lets every model get a working CRUD list page with no per-model template work, at the cost of showing only the model's __str__ instead of domain columns, so any screen that needs real columns must be forked into a bespoke template.

nodes.label: Shared Record Form Scaffold
nodes.rationale: One create/edit form body (Edit-vs-Add title driven by presence of 'object', object_label fallback of 'record', csrf token, multipart enctype, partials/_form_fields.html for field rendering, Save plus history.back() Cancel) is duplicated per app. novalidate defers validation to Django server-side forms rather than the browser; history.back() avoids having to know a per-model success/cancel URL.

nodes.label: URL-Name Derived Page Title
nodes.rationale: Page heading and title are computed at render time from request.resolver_match.url_name with the '_list' suffix cut and title-cased, so one shared template self-labels for every route that renders it. This is what makes the generic list scaffold reusable without a per-view context variable, but it couples display text to URL naming conventions.

nodes.label: Role-Based UI Action Gating
nodes.rationale: Mutating actions (Add item, Stock movement, Edit, Register device, Save review) are wrapped in template-level checks on user.is_superuser and user.role against ADMIN/OWNER/MANAGER/VET. Inventory allows MANAGER while IoT device registration is restricted to ADMIN/OWNER only, and health review is gated to VET, encoding a per-domain privilege ladder. This is presentation-layer hiding only and must be mirrored by view-level permission checks to be a real control.

nodes.label: Severity Badge Convention
nodes.rationale: Health observation severity is rendered as a 'sev-{{ severity }}' CSS class plus get_severity_display() label, so the stylesheet owns the colour mapping and the template stays agnostic to the choice set.

nodes.label: Device Online/Offline Status Badge
nodes.rationale: Device liveness is surfaced from an is_online model property into a status-ok / status-muted badge, alongside a separate get_status_display() lifecycle status and last_seen_at fallback of 'never' — administrative status and heartbeat liveness are kept as two distinct signals.

nodes.label: Veterinary Review Workflow
nodes.rationale: An observation detail page carries a second, separately-posted review form (health:observation_review) rendered only for reviewers, recording reviewed_by, reviewed_at and vet_comment. The observation may also link to a vision inference result (vision:result_detail on vision_result.result_uuid), making the vet the human-in-the-loop confirmation step over automated image classification.

nodes.label: Low Stock Reorder Signal
nodes.rationale: current_stock is compared against reorder_level via an is_low_stock property and surfaced as a Low/OK badge plus a '?low=1' filter link, so replenishment urgency is computed on the model and only displayed by the template.

nodes.label: Environment Chart Data Fetch
nodes.rationale: The device detail page draws a 7-day temperature and humidity line chart by making two nested JSON fetches to iot:sensor_chart_data (metric=temperature, metric=humidity) keyed on device_id, then feeding both series into one Chart.js line chart. Chart data is fetched asynchronously rather than rendered into the template context so the page can load before sensor history is aggregated.

nodes.label: Detail Page Stat Tile Pattern
nodes.rationale: Detail pages open with a row of dashboard/_stat.html includes (label/value/icon) summarising the entity's key numbers before the child-record table, reusing the dashboard KPI component outside the dashboard.

nodes.label: YOLO Class to Risk Category Mapping
nodes.rationale: A configurable YAML mapping decouples the detector's class vocabulary from the web application's alert taxonomy, so risk categories, severities and alert types can be re-tuned without retraining or changing application code.
nodes.norm_label: yolo class to risk category mapping

nodes.label: yolo11n Detector (Configured Default Model)
nodes.rationale: Chosen as a lightweight nano detector to keep training reproducible and to allow deployment on edge hardware (Raspberry Pi class devices) rather than maximising raw accuracy.

nodes.label: MODEL_CARD.md Trained Model Record
nodes.rationale: The final trained model and its version are recorded in ml/models/MODEL_CARD.md after training on real data, so the config default is explicitly not the provenance record.

nodes.label: healthy Class
nodes.rationale: Maps to the normal risk category with severity information and a null alert_type, so healthy detections are recorded but never raise an alert.

nodes.label: open_beak_stress Class
nodes.rationale: Open-beak posture is treated as a heat/respiratory distress indicator and is given its own warning-level alert type rather than being folded into a generic abnormality category.

nodes.label: slipped_tendon Class
nodes.rationale: The only class assigned critical severity, reflecting that a mobility abnormality is a welfare emergency requiring immediate stockperson intervention rather than routine monitoring.

nodes.label: Supplementary (Not Yet Trainable) Classes
nodes.rationale: Documented in the mapping so the alert taxonomy is complete and configurable, but explicitly excluded from training because no labelled data exists for them; enabling them without data would silently produce untrained, unreliable classes.

nodes.label: uncertain Review Outcome
nodes.rationale: Deliberately modelled as an inference/review OUTCOME rather than a trained class, so low-confidence detections route to human review instead of being predicted as a category the detector was never trained on.

nodes.label: Alert Severity Scale (information | warning | critical)
nodes.rationale: Severity strings in this YAML must match apps.alerts.models.Severity exactly, making the config a shared contract between the ML pipeline and the Django alerts app.

nodes.label: default_severity Fallback
nodes.rationale: Defaults to warning so a class that maps to an alert but omits severity still produces an actionable, non-silent alert rather than being dropped or escalated to critical.

nodes.label: alert_type Web Application Contract
nodes.rationale: Risk categories are mapped onto alert types owned by the web application, so the detector never emits UI-facing alert names directly; a null alert_type is the explicit way to say 'detected but do not alert'.

nodes.label: YOLO Training Configuration
nodes.rationale: Centralises hyperparameters in one declarative file so Colab runs and local runs stay identical apart from path overrides.

nodes.label: yolo11n.pt Pretrained Weights
nodes.rationale: Lightweight nano detector selected as the documented default, matching the edge-deployment constraint of the monitoring hardware.

nodes.label: Conservative Biologically-Realistic Augmentation Policy
nodes.rationale: Augmentation is deliberately restrained (limited rotation, limited scaling, moderate HSV) so synthetic images still depict postures a real bird can adopt; aggressive augmentation would teach the detector impossible poultry appearances and corrupt welfare-behaviour classes.

nodes.label: Vertical Flip Disabled (flipud = 0.0)
nodes.rationale: Explicitly never vertical-flip a bird: an upside-down bird is not a valid real-world observation, and inverting images would destroy the posture cues that distinguish healthy from lethargic or mobility-abnormal birds.

nodes.label: Horizontal Flip Augmentation (fliplr = 0.5)
nodes.rationale: Left-right mirroring is retained because a bird facing either direction is equally plausible in a pen.

nodes.label: Early Stopping (patience = 20)
nodes.rationale: Caps wasted Colab GPU time and guards against overfitting on a small labelled poultry dataset by stopping once validation stops improving for 20 epochs of the 100 budgeted.

nodes.label: Deterministic Seed (seed = 42)
nodes.rationale: Fixed seed makes runs reproducible 'where possible' — an explicit acknowledgement that GPU nondeterminism means bit-exact reproduction is not guaranteed, only approximate repeatability for the dissertation results.

nodes.label: Environment Variable Path Overrides (DATASET_YAML, PROJECT_DIR)
nodes.rationale: Lets the same committed config run unchanged in Colab where dataset and output paths differ, avoiding per-environment forks of the config file.

nodes.label: MixUp Disabled (mixup = 0.0)
nodes.rationale: Blending two images would create ghosted, semi-transparent birds that no camera could observe, so mixup is switched off under the biological-realism constraint.

nodes.label: Heat Stress in Poultry (Multi-Domain Impact Diagram)
nodes.rationale: Conceptual figure showing solar/thermal load falling on a chicken and radiating into four consequence domains (behavioral, physiological, neuroendocrine, production). It frames heat stress as a whole-bird syndrome rather than a single measurable variable, which motivates multi-modal sensing (temperature, humidity, behavior, acoustics) instead of a single thermometer.
nodes.norm_label: heat stress in poultry (multi-domain impact diagram)

nodes.label: Behavioral Changes Under Heat Stress
nodes.rationale: Listed as: less time feeding, more time drinking, panting, less moving/walking, wings elevated. These are externally observable, which makes them the cheapest signals for camera/microphone-based detection.

nodes.label: Physiological Changes Under Heat Stress
nodes.rationale: Oxidative stress, acid-base imbalance, respiratory alkalosis, increased H/L ratio, altered cecal microbial profile. These require invasive/lab sampling, so they are ground-truth references rather than deployable sensors.

nodes.label: Neuroendocrine Changes Under Heat Stress
nodes.rationale: Up: CRF, ACTH, catecholamines, plasma corticosterone. Down: T3, GnRH, FSH and LH. Shows the HPA axis activation plus reproductive-axis suppression that explains fertility and egg losses.

nodes.label: Production Changes Under Heat Stress
nodes.rationale: Increased mortality, decreased feed intake, poor FCR, reduced body weight, lower meat quality, fewer/poorer eggs. This is the economic endpoint that justifies early-warning monitoring.

nodes.label: Panting (Thermoregulatory Behavior)
nodes.rationale: Evaporative cooling response; it is the behavioral link to respiratory alkalosis and is acoustically and visually detectable.

nodes.label: Heterophil/Lymphocyte (H/L) Ratio
nodes.rationale: Presented as a physiological stress index; used as an objective validation marker against which non-invasive stress proxies can be calibrated.

nodes.label: Reduced Feed Intake
nodes.rationale: Appears in both behavioral (spend less time feeding) and production (decreased feed intake) lists, making it the bridge between observable behavior and economic loss.

nodes.label: Raspberry Pi Single-Board Computer
nodes.rationale: Product photograph of a Raspberry Pi Model B-class board (Samsung LPDDR SDRAM package, Broadcom SoC, 40-pin GPIO header, 4x USB, Ethernet, HDMI, CSI camera connector, micro-USB power, 3.5mm AV jack). Included as the reference low-cost compute platform for on-farm edge deployment: it is cheap, low-power, has a native camera interface and GPIO for environmental sensors, which is why it is preferred over a PC or a pure-cloud design in resource-constrained poultry houses.

nodes.label: 40-Pin GPIO Header
nodes.rationale: The physical attachment point for temperature, humidity, CO2 and NH3 sensor breakouts; it is what makes the board a sensor hub rather than just a computer.

nodes.label: Low-Cost Edge Computing Hardware Choice
nodes.rationale: Trade-off captured by the figure: commodity SBC hardware trades raw inference throughput for price, power draw, ruggedness and replaceability, which suits poultry houses with intermittent connectivity where sending raw video to the cloud is infeasible.

nodes.label: Smart Poultry Farm System Architecture (Edge - Platform - Portals)
nodes.rationale: Three-tier block diagram partitioning the system into an Edge Subsystem, a Digital Farming Platform and Portals. The split exists so that latency-sensitive and bandwidth-heavy vision work stays at the edge while aggregation, storage and user-facing logic live centrally; markers 1 and 2 highlight the AI-bearing blocks.
nodes.norm_label: smart poultry farm system architecture (edge - platform - portals)

nodes.label: IoT Nodes with Sensors (Microphone, Air Temp, Humidity, CO2, NH3, Light)
nodes.rationale: Sensor set chosen to cover the whole poultry-house microclimate: thermal comfort (temperature, humidity), air quality (CO2, NH3), lighting regime, and acoustics for vocalisation-based stress cues.
nodes.norm_label: iot nodes with sensors (microphone, air temp, humidity, co2, nh3, light)

nodes.label: Smart IoT Camera Nodes
nodes.rationale: Cameras are paired one-to-one with edge devices so inference happens next to the sensor; only results, not raw video, traverse the Ethernet/4G links.

nodes.label: IoT Edge Gateway
nodes.rationale: Single aggregation and protocol-translation point: it speaks BLE/LoRa/Ethernet downstream to heterogeneous nodes and 4G upstream, so the cloud sees one uniform stream and rural sites need only one WAN link.

nodes.label: IoT Platform (Gateway, Sensor Data, Node Configuration, Security)
nodes.norm_label: iot platform (gateway, sensor data, node configuration, security)

nodes.label: Farm Management Services
nodes.rationale: Bundles incident detection, reporting, service book, admin, alert hub, map configuration, integration, environment monitoring, acoustic stress detection and food mix optimization into one service layer so analytics and workflow share the same sensor context.

nodes.label: Stress Detection (Acoustic)
nodes.rationale: Audio is used as a stress channel because vocalisation and panting sounds carry flock-level state at far lower bandwidth than video.

nodes.label: Chicken Weight Estimation
nodes.rationale: Vision-based weighing removes the handling stress and labour of manual weighing while giving continuous growth curves.

nodes.label: Data Storage (Blob Storage + SQL Database)
nodes.source_location: Digital Farming Platform, right grey column
nodes.rationale: Polyglot persistence: blob storage for images/audio and a relational database for structured telemetry and farm records.

nodes.label: User Portal App Logic / Web-Mobile API / 3rd-Party API

nodes.rationale: Three distinct human roles get three distinct front ends: continuous supervision, in-house walk-around inspection, and system administration.
nodes.norm_label: portals (command center, mobile inspection app, admin portal)

nodes.label: Infrared Thermography Panel of Broiler Chickens
nodes.rationale: Research figure arranged as a 4-row x 5-column matrix over five birds/sessions: row A whole-body thermograms with a global temperature reading (36.8, 35.8, 36.5, 29.1, 31.9 C) and a scale bar, row B the matching RGB photographs with a coloured ROI box, row C the cropped thermal ROI with Avg/High/Low statistics, row D the same ROI rendered as a segmented/contoured false-colour map. It demonstrates the pipeline from raw thermogram to region-level temperature statistics.
nodes.norm_label: infrared thermography panel of broiler chickens

nodes.label: Thermal Region-of-Interest Extraction
nodes.source_location: rows B and C, coloured bounding boxes
nodes.rationale: A bounding box is drawn on the visible-light frame and transferred to the co-registered thermogram, so temperature is read from a defined body region rather than from the whole frame including litter and equipment.

nodes.label: Avg/High/Low Surface Temperature Statistics
nodes.source_location: captions under rows C and D
nodes.rationale: Reducing an ROI to average, maximum and minimum temperature gives a compact, comparable feature vector; the spread between high and low is itself a thermoregulation cue. Reported values range roughly 25.8-40.9 C across the five subjects.

nodes.label: Paired RGB and Thermal Image Registration
nodes.rationale: RGB gives the semantics (which pixels are bird) and the thermal channel gives the measurement; pairing them is what makes automated, repeatable body-region thermometry possible.
nodes.norm_label: paired rgb and thermal image registration

nodes.label: Segmented False-Colour Thermal Map
nodes.rationale: Row D shows contour/point-cloud style segmentation over the ROI, isolating the hot core (comb, wattle, featherless skin) from cooler feathered areas. Exact segmentation algorithm is not stated in the figure.

nodes.label: YOLO Unified Object Detection Model
nodes.rationale: The canonical YOLO system diagram (dog/bicycle/car scene): the input is divided by an SxS grid, one branch predicts bounding boxes plus confidence, a parallel branch predicts a class probability map, and the two are combined into final detections. The design rationale is that detection is reframed as a single regression over the whole image, giving one-pass real-time inference instead of a region-proposal plus classification cascade.

nodes.label: S x S Grid on Input
nodes.rationale: Each grid cell is made responsible for objects whose centre falls in it, which is what makes the number of predictions fixed and the network fully convolutional.
nodes.norm_label: s x s grid on input

nodes.label: Bounding Boxes + Confidence Prediction
nodes.rationale: Box thickness in the figure encodes confidence; low-confidence boxes are later suppressed, which is the mechanism that turns a dense box field into a sparse detection set.

nodes.label: Class Probability Map
nodes.rationale: Per-cell conditional class probabilities are predicted independently of the boxes and only multiplied in at the end, so the class head sees global image context.

nodes.label: Final Detections
nodes.rationale: Result of combining box confidence with class probabilities and thresholding/NMS; the figure shows three surviving boxes (dog, bicycle, car).

nodes.label: Poultry Fecal Mobile Data-Collection App
nodes.rationale: Three-panel figure: two ODK/form-style Android screens flanking a field photograph of an enumerator photographing chickens with a smartphone. The app is a single scrolling form (clipboard icon, save and finalise actions in the app bar) that couples image capture, a mutually exclusive disease label, free-text observations and a GPS fix into one submitted record. The design decision is to have the annotation happen in the field at capture time rather than in a later desk-based labelling pass.

nodes.label: Fecal Image Capture (Take Picture / Choose Image)
nodes.rationale: Offering both live capture and gallery selection lets the same form serve fresh field collection and retrospective upload.
nodes.norm_label: fecal image capture (take picture / choose image)

nodes.label: Disease Class Radio Selection (Healthy, Coccidiosis, Newcastle, Salmonella, Other)
nodes.source_location: left and right panels, Type of Image section
nodes.rationale: Radio buttons enforce a single mutually exclusive label per image, which is exactly the target format for supervised single-label classification; 'Other' is the escape hatch that prevents forced mislabelling.
nodes.norm_label: disease class radio selection (healthy, coccidiosis, newcastle, salmonella, other)

nodes.label: GPS Reading / Start GeoPoint
nodes.rationale: Geotagging every sample enables spatial outbreak mapping and prevents duplicate/farm-confounded records; the 'please wait until phone gets reading' hint acknowledges GPS lock latency in the field.

nodes.label: In-Field Labelled Dataset Collection Strategy
nodes.rationale: Using a smartphone form as the acquisition instrument trades image quality control (variable lighting, backgrounds, handheld framing) for scale, low cost and expert-at-source labels. The centre photograph documents the realistic, cluttered capture conditions the resulting model must tolerate.

nodes.description: Circular institutional emblem (gold ring on dark blue) of The University of Bamenda / Universite de Bamenda, Cameroon. Inner roundel shows a green mountain landscape (the Bamenda highlands) with an open white book and the abbreviation 'UBa' on a scroll; a banner across the base carries the motto. nodes.label: Motto: Knowledge, Probity, Entrepreneurship
nodes.description: Three-word institutional motto rendered on the banner at the foot of the seal, stating the university's declared values.
nodes.rationale: Placed on the outer banner (the most legible band of a small seal) so the values remain readable when the emblem is reduced to letterhead or thumbnail size.

nodes.label: Bilingual English/French Institutional Identity
nodes.description: The seal carries the institution's name twice, in English on the upper arc ('THE UNIVERSITY OF BAMENDA') and in French on the lower arc ('UNIVERSITE DE BAMENDA').
nodes.rationale: Duplicating the name in both official languages of Cameroon on a single ring makes the mark valid for documents submitted in either language, avoiding the need for two separate logos; the design cost is that the ring text is small and the two arcs mirror each other.

nodes.label: Overhead Broiler House Frame (Siren, 2022-02-26 23:11:10)
nodes.description: Colour CCTV still shot near-vertically down onto the litter floor of a commercial broiler house. Several hundred mid-growth white birds are spread over a dusty grey floor at moderate density, with a horizontal blue feed pipe crossing the frame carrying five red-capped suspended pan feeders. On-screen text reads '1080P-IPC-Siren' (top left) and '2022-02-26 23:11:10' (top right). This is a sampled training/inspection frame for flock behaviour analysis, not a photograph of an individual bird.

nodes.label: Siren Camera Channel Label
nodes.description: The burned-in camera identifier '1080P-IPC-Siren' appearing in the upper-left of most frames. The suffix names an experimental stimulus/alarm condition rather than a location, so the channel name doubles as a per-frame condition label recoverable straight from the pixels.
nodes.rationale: Encoding the condition in the IP camera's display name means every exported frame is self-labelled even when the video files are renamed or re-cut, which removes the need for a separate side-car label file; the cost is that the label is permanently baked into the image region and becomes a spurious cue a model can latch onto.

nodes.label: Suspended Pan Feeder Line
nodes.description: The fixed horizontal feed pipe and its row of five red-and-white circular pan feeders that bisect every frame at roughly the same image height. Because the camera is rigidly mounted, this line is a static spatial landmark that can serve as a reference for calibrating scale and for defining a feeding zone region-of-interest.

nodes.label: Dense Flock Overhead Frame (Siren, 2022-03-01 22:59:59)
nodes.description: Colour overhead still from the same fixed camera three days later than frame00001, labelled '1080P-IPC-Siren' and '2022-03-01 22:59:59'. Birds are visibly larger and the floor is far more densely covered; individual birds already touch and partially overlap, and rings of birds have formed around each pan feeder. The feed line sits at the same image height, confirming the camera has not moved between sessions.

nodes.label: Feeder Aggregation Behaviour
nodes.description: The visible pattern of birds forming dense radial clusters immediately around each pan feeder while the floor between feeders stays comparatively open. This spatial aggregation is the observable behaviour signal the dataset is built to quantify: feeding activity can be estimated from bird density inside a feeder region without ever tracking an individual animal.
nodes.rationale: Measuring aggregation at the flock level sidesteps the identity problem entirely - individual re-identification is infeasible in a crowd of near-identical white birds seen from above, whereas an occupancy count around a fixed feeder is robust to occlusion and needs no per-bird annotation.

nodes.label: Near-Market-Weight Flock Frame (Gas, 2022-03-14 22:24:07)
nodes.description: Bright colour overhead still labelled '1080P-IPC-Gas' and '2022-03-14 22:24:07'. Large, near-market-weight broilers cover almost the entire floor; only narrow strips of bare litter remain. Birds are packed shoulder to shoulder in tight fans radiating from each of the five pan feeders, and the feed pipe is partly hidden by birds standing beneath it.

nodes.label: Gas Camera Channel Label
nodes.description: The burned-in camera identifier '1080P-IPC-Gas', the second observed channel/condition name in the dataset alongside the Siren channel. Its presence shows the frame set spans at least two named environmental conditions captured by the same overhead rig.

nodes.label: Severe Occlusion at High Stocking Density
nodes.description: At late growth stage the birds tile the floor almost completely, so silhouettes merge into a continuous white mass with no separating background between neighbours.
nodes.rationale: This is why a detector trained only on early sparse frames will collapse on late frames: bounding-box detection assumes separable instances, an assumption that fails once the floor coverage approaches saturation. It argues for density/segmentation-style estimation or for stratifying training data across growth stages instead of sampling frames uniformly in time.
nodes.norm_label: severe occlusion at high stocking density

nodes.label: Infrared Night-Mode Frame (Siren, 2022-02-22 08:14:11)
nodes.description: Monochrome (infrared night-vision) overhead still labelled '1080P-IPC-Siren' and '2022-02-22 08:14:11'. The scene is entirely greyscale: the normally red feeder caps appear dark grey and the litter is a mottled grey field. Birds are small young chicks scattered sparsely, with clear bare floor between most individuals and loose rings around the feeders. Motion blur on several chicks indicates a long exposure under low light.

nodes.label: Greyscale IR vs Colour Domain Shift
nodes.description: The same camera switches automatically between colour daylight capture and monochrome infrared capture, so the dataset contains two visually distinct imaging domains of one physical scene.
nodes.rationale: Any pipeline that relies on colour cues - for example locating the bright red feeder caps to anchor the feeding zone, or separating white birds from grey litter by saturation - silently loses that cue on IR frames. The practical consequences are that anchors must be geometric rather than chromatic, and that colour-jitter or grayscale augmentation is needed so a single model covers both domains instead of training two.
nodes.norm_label: greyscale ir vs colour domain shift

nodes.label: Early Growth Stage Flock
nodes.description: The earliest-dated observation in this chunk (22 February): small chicks occupying only a fraction of the floor area, well separated, giving the cleanest instance separation of any frame here. Apparent bird size in pixels is therefore a proxy for age within the production cycle.

nodes.label: Late Growth Flock Frame (Siren, 2022-03-14 22:12:23)
nodes.description: Colour overhead still labelled '1080P-IPC-Siren' and '2022-03-14 22:12:23' - the same calendar day as the Gas-channel frame but twelve minutes earlier. Large birds crowd the floor with only thin channels of visible litter, and dense fans of birds press against each pan feeder along the grey feed pipe.

nodes.label: Burned-In Timestamp OSD Overlay
nodes.description: The white on-screen-display date/time string rendered by the DVR into the top-right corner of every frame (here '2022-03-14 22:12:23'). Combined with the channel name in the opposite corner it makes each exported PNG fully self-describing in time and condition.
nodes.rationale: Baking the clock into the pixels survives frame extraction, renaming and re-encoding, so temporal ordering can be recovered even when the sequential filenames (frame00001, frame00101, frame00201, frame00401) do not follow chronological order - which they demonstrably do not here. The trade-off is a permanently corrupted image region that should be cropped or masked before training.

nodes.label: Growth Progression Across the Production Cycle
nodes.description: Across the sampled dates (22 Feb, 26 Feb, 1 Mar, 14 Mar 2022) from one fixed viewpoint, mean bird size in pixels and floor coverage increase monotonically while inter-bird spacing collapses. The frame set therefore forms a longitudinal record of a single broiler production cycle rather than a set of independent scenes.
nodes.rationale: Holding the camera pose constant is what makes the comparison meaningful: because viewpoint, feeder positions and scale are unchanged, differences between frames can be attributed to the flock itself instead of to camera movement, which is what allows density and size to be read as growth indicators.
nodes.norm_label: growth progression across the production cycle

nodes.label: PIR Camera Night Flock Frame (2022-02-27 23:43:07)
nodes.description: Overhead CCTV still from a commercial broiler house, captured by the camera channel labelled '1080P-IPC-PIR' at 2022-02-27 23:43:07. Several hundred white broilers of intermediate size are spread across a bare earth/litter floor. A suspended grey feed-conveyor pipe runs diagonally across the frame with five red-topped tube pan feeders hanging from it; birds ring the pans in dense clusters while the open floor areas hold more loosely scattered, mostly sitting birds. A red drinker bell is visible bottom-left and a glowing orange heat source (brooder/heater vent) sits at the right edge. This is a raw training/inference frame for chicken behaviour analysis, not a chart or UI.

nodes.label: Brooder Heat Source / Glowing Heater Vent
nodes.description: A bright orange glowing element at the right edge of the PIR-camera frames, consistent with a gas brooder / heater flame port in the poultry house wall. It is a fixed bright region that saturates the sensor and creates a persistent hotspot, which matters for detection models because it is a static high-contrast distractor that never moves between frames.
nodes.rationale: Heat sources are a known confounder in poultry CCTV analytics: they cause local overexposure and thermal-glow artefacts that a naive motion or brightness-based detector can mistake for activity, so behaviour models must either mask this region or rely on appearance-based detection.
nodes.norm_label: brooder heat source / glowing heater vent

nodes.label: 1080P-IPC-PIR Camera Channel
nodes.description: One of at least three named 1080p IP camera channels in the dataset, burned into the top-left of the frame as '1080P-IPC-PIR'. This channel views the pen from a shallower, more oblique angle than the others and includes the heater wall and a red bell drinker in view.

nodes.label: Burned-In Timestamp and Camera-Label Overlay
nodes.description: Every frame in this chunk carries a top-right date-time stamp (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS) and a top-left camera identifier. Together these give each still an implicit (camera, timestamp) key, which is what allows frames to be ordered into behaviour sequences and grouped by bird age and time-of-day without any separate metadata file.
nodes.rationale: The overlay is the only source of provenance for these stills, so it doubles as the dataset's de-facto index; it is also a fixed white-on-dark region that should be cropped or masked before training so the model does not key on rendered digits.

nodes.label: Elevated Overhead Wide-Angle Viewpoint
nodes.description: All frames are shot from a ceiling-mounted wide-angle lens looking down and across the pen, producing visible barrel distortion (the floor cable and pen edge bow into arcs) and a strong scale gradient: birds near the top of the frame are much smaller in pixels than birds at the bottom. Individuals appear as top-down feathered ovals with no visible head-on silhouette.
nodes.rationale: The top-down view is chosen because it minimises occlusion between densely stocked birds and gives near-complete pen coverage from one camera, at the cost of losing the side profile cues (posture, leg extension) that a ground-level camera would give — so behaviour must be inferred from footprint shape, spacing and motion rather than pose.

nodes.label: Gas Camera Daytime Flock Frame (2022-02-23 11:00:32)
nodes.description: Colour overhead still from the '1080P-IPC-Gas' channel at 2022-02-23 11:00:32. Birds are noticeably smaller and paler than in the March frames, consistent with an earlier point in the grow-out cycle. A horizontal feed pipe crosses mid-frame with four red-topped pan feeders; birds form tight rosettes around each pan while the lower third of the floor is nearly empty. Feed is visibly present in the pans.

nodes.label: 1080P-IPC-Gas Camera Channel
nodes.description: Camera channel labelled '1080P-IPC-Gas', viewing a feeder line almost perpendicular to the lens axis so the pipe runs left-to-right across the middle of the frame. Appears in both the February and March frames of this chunk, providing a fixed viewpoint across which bird growth can be compared.

nodes.label: Suspended Pan Feeder Line
nodes.description: The dominant fixed structure in every frame: a horizontal feed-conveyor pipe carrying evenly spaced circular pan feeders with red conical tops and white grill spokes. Because the pans are rigidly spaced and never move, they act as natural spatial anchors and as regions of interest for scoring feeding behaviour and feeder occupancy.
nodes.rationale: Anchoring behaviour analysis to the feeder line is attractive because the equipment geometry is constant across all cameras and dates, so feeder-zone occupancy can be counted without any per-frame calibration; the red pan tops also give a strong colour cue for automatic localisation in the daylight/colour frames.

nodes.label: Early Grow-Out Stage (Small Birds, Late February)
nodes.description: In the 22-27 February frames each bird occupies a small fraction of the pan-feeder diameter, and large areas of bare floor remain visible between birds. This gives a low apparent stocking density and well-separated individual blobs, which is the easiest regime for individual detection and tracking.
nodes.norm_label: early grow-out stage (small birds, late february)

nodes.label: Siren Camera Infrared Flock Frame (2022-02-22 08:53:45)
nodes.description: Monochrome infrared still from the '1080P-IPC-Siren' channel at 2022-02-22 08:53:45. Despite the morning timestamp the camera is in IR night mode, so the scene is greyscale with the red feeder tops rendered as neutral grey. Small birds are scattered fairly evenly with loose aggregations in the upper right; five pan feeders hang from a horizontal pipe and a floor cable arcs across the lower third.

nodes.label: 1080P-IPC-Siren Camera Channel
nodes.description: Camera channel labelled '1080P-IPC-Siren'. Both of its frames in this chunk are greyscale IR captures showing the same five-pan feeder line and the same floor cable arc, confirming a fixed mount and a consistent field of view across days.

nodes.label: Infrared / Low-Light Monochrome Capture Mode
nodes.description: When house lighting is dim the cameras switch to IR illumination and emit single-channel greyscale frames with flattened contrast between birds and litter. Colour cues that identify feeders and drinkers in daylight frames disappear entirely, and bird outlines merge into the substrate.
nodes.rationale: The dataset therefore contains two visually distinct domains from the same physical scene; a detector trained only on the colour frames will degrade on the IR frames, which argues for greyscale augmentation or explicit day/night domain handling rather than a single colour-dependent pipeline.

nodes.label: Siren Camera Infrared Night Frame (2022-02-24 22:00:00)
nodes.description: Monochrome IR still from the '1080P-IPC-Siren' channel at 2022-02-24 22:00:00, same fixed viewpoint as frame00801. Birds are markedly more aggregated here: dense rosettes press around each of the four visible pan feeders and a large clump fills the upper right, while wide stretches of floor in the lower half are empty. The contrast with the 08:53 frame from the same camera makes this a natural pair for studying diurnal redistribution.

nodes.label: Feeder-Centred Clustering Behaviour
nodes.description: The recurring observable behaviour across all six frames: birds form near-circular rosettes radiating outward from each pan feeder, bodies pointing inward toward the pan rim. Rosette thickness (how many concentric rings of birds surround a pan) varies strongly between frames and is the most legible behavioural signal available from the overhead view.
nodes.rationale: Feeder rosette density is a useful proxy for feeding activity precisely because it is measurable without individual tracking — a per-pan radial occupancy count survives the heavy occlusion and low resolution that defeat per-bird identity tracking in a densely stocked house.

nodes.label: Resting / Sitting Distribution on Open Floor
nodes.description: Away from the feeder line, birds appear as motionless rounded blobs with tucked outlines rather than the elongated shape of a walking bird, and they are distributed in loose patches with bare floor between them. Distinguishing this resting state from feeding is the second behavioural class the overhead footage can support.
nodes.norm_label: resting / sitting distribution on open floor

nodes.label: Gas Camera Mature Broiler Frame (2022-03-14 22:25:42)
nodes.description: Colour overhead still from the '1080P-IPC-Gas' channel at 2022-03-14 22:25:42, nineteen days after frame00501 from the same camera. The birds are now large, plump and heavily feathered, filling almost the entire floor with barely any visible litter between bodies. Five red-topped pan feeders remain on the same pipe but each bird now spans roughly the pan diameter, so only a handful of birds fit around each pan. Bodies overlap and merge visually.

nodes.label: Late Grow-Out Stage (Large Birds, Mid-March)
nodes.description: By mid-March the same pen holds birds several times the pixel area they occupied in February, measured against the unchanged pan-feeder diameter. The feeder equipment acts as an in-frame scale reference that makes this growth directly quantifiable from the imagery alone.

nodes.label: High Apparent Stocking Density and Occlusion
nodes.description: In the late-cycle frame adjacent birds touch and overlap so that the flock reads as a continuous white mass with only faint seams between individuals; the floor is almost fully covered. Individual instance boundaries are frequently indeterminate.
nodes.rationale: This is the hardest regime for the pipeline: bounding-box detection and identity tracking break down when instances merge, which pushes the analysis toward density estimation, segmentation or region-occupancy counting rather than per-bird detection for late-cycle footage.
nodes.norm_label: high apparent stocking density and occlusion

nodes.label: PIR Camera Night Flock Frame (2022-02-27 23:44:26)
nodes.description: Colour overhead still from the '1080P-IPC-PIR' channel at 2022-02-27 23:44:26, seventy-nine seconds after frame004011 from the same camera. The scene is identical in structure — same diagonal feed pipe, same five red-topped pans, same red bell drinker bottom-left, same glowing heater at the right — but individual birds have shifted position and the rosettes around the pans have thinned, showing measurable short-interval movement.

nodes.label: Short-Interval Temporal Frame Pair
nodes.description: Two stills from the same camera separated by about 79 seconds (23:43:07 and 23:44:26 on 2022-02-27) with static equipment and shifted birds. Because everything except the animals is pixel-stable, differencing the pair isolates flock movement and gives a ready-made activity signal.
nodes.rationale: Extracting near-consecutive frames rather than isolated stills is what makes motion-based activity indices possible at all; with a fixed mount the background subtracts cleanly, so no registration step is needed and residual motion can be attributed directly to the birds.

nodes.label: Frame 02101: Daytime Colour Overhead View of Dense Broiler Flock at Feeder Line
nodes.rationale: Ceiling-mounted colour CCTV still from a commercial broiler house, camera label '1080P-IPC-Siren', timestamp overlay 2022-03-14 22:13:57. Shows several hundred near-market-weight white broilers packed almost wall-to-wall on damp litter. A horizontal grey feed conveyor pipe crosses the frame with five red-capped circular pan feeders suspended from it; each pan holds visible feed and is ringed by birds head-in, producing the classic radial feeding cluster. Bird density is far higher and body size far larger than in the February frames, marking a late point in the grow-out cycle.
nodes.norm_label: frame 02101: daytime colour overhead view of dense broiler flock at feeder line

nodes.label: Frame 02501: Infrared Night View of Young Broilers with Sparse Feeder Attendance
nodes.rationale: Monochrome infrared/low-light CCTV still, '1080P-IPC-Siren', 2022-02-22 08:16:19. Smaller, younger birds are loosely scattered in patchy clumps across a broad litter floor; the five pan feeders on the crossing feed line appear largely empty of feed, with only partial rings of birds attending them. The house perimeter wall and a floor-level cable/curtain line are visible at the bottom of the frame, and the wide-angle lens produces noticeable barrel distortion.
nodes.norm_label: frame 02501: infrared night view of young broilers with sparse feeder attendance

nodes.label: Frame 025501: Infrared View of Flock Dispersed Away From Empty Feed Pans
nodes.rationale: Monochrome infrared CCTV still, '1080P-IPC-Siren', 2022-02-22 08:55:26, roughly 39 minutes after frame02501 from the same camera and same flock. Birds have re-aggregated into two large drifts on the left and right of the frame, leaving a conspicuous empty aisle of bare litter through the middle beneath the feed line; the pan feeders are empty and almost unattended. The near-identical viewpoint and short time gap make this frame a natural temporal pair with frame02501 for studying flock redistribution between feeding bouts.
nodes.norm_label: frame 025501: infrared view of flock dispersed away from empty feed pans

nodes.label: Frame 02701: Gas-Zone Camera View of Young Broilers Crowding Filled Feeders
nodes.rationale: Daytime colour CCTV still, camera label '1080P-IPC-Gas' (a different house zone from the 'Siren' camera), 2022-02-23 11:02:35. Young white broilers form a broad wedge-shaped mass in the upper half of the frame and tight rings around four red-capped pan feeders that contain visible brown feed. A conical brooder/gas heater canopy intrudes at the top-right corner, and floor cables run across the lower litter area. The distinct camera identifier confirms the dataset spans multiple viewpoints within the same facility.
nodes.norm_label: frame 02701: gas-zone camera view of young broilers crowding filled feeders

nodes.label: Frame 03201: Overhead View of Mid-Growth Broilers Feeding From Filled Pans
nodes.rationale: Daytime colour CCTV still, '1080P-IPC-Siren', 2022-03-01 23:02:44. Mid-grow-out birds cover the whole floor at moderate-to-high density on wet, trodden litter. Five pan feeders hang from the grey feed pipe with pale feed clearly visible in each pan and birds pressed head-in around them, while many other birds sit or rest away from the line. Bird size is intermediate between the February frames and frame02101, giving this frame a middle position in the growth timeline.
nodes.norm_label: frame 03201: overhead view of mid-growth broilers feeding from filled pans

nodes.label: Frame 03801: Infrared View of Radial Feeding Rosettes Around Pan Feeders
nodes.rationale: Monochrome infrared CCTV still, '1080P-IPC-Siren', 2022-02-24 22:03:11. The clearest example in this chunk of the radial 'rosette' geometry: birds arranged spoke-like with bodies pointing outward and heads into each pan feeder, forming near-circular petal patterns around the central and flanking pans. Surrounding floor area is comparatively sparse, making the feeder-attendance signal visually separable from ambient loafing behaviour.
nodes.norm_label: frame 03801: infrared view of radial feeding rosettes around pan feeders

nodes.label: Overhead Broiler-House CCTV Surveillance Frame
nodes.rationale: All frames in this chunk share one acquisition modality: a fixed 1080p wide-angle IP camera mounted in the ceiling of a commercial broiler house, looking near-vertically down at the litter floor. The fixed viewpoint means background (feed line, walls, cables) is static across frames, so only the birds move — a property that makes simple background/foreground and density-based methods viable alongside detection models.

nodes.label: Suspended Pan Feeder Line
nodes.rationale: A horizontal conveyor pipe crossing every frame, carrying four to five circular pan feeders with red caps (colour frames) or pale grey grilles (infrared frames).
