It is the single most stable landmark in the scene and effectively defines the region of interest for feeding-behaviour analysis: bird positions are meaningful mainly relative to these fixed pan centres.

nodes.label: Feeding Cluster at Feeder Pan
nodes.rationale: The recurring behavioural unit visible from above: a compact ring of birds pressed against a pan with heads inward. Because the overhead view hides beaks and heads under the pan rim, the cluster geometry itself — not the head pose — is the observable cue that feeding is occurring.

nodes.label: Radial Feeder Rosette Formation
nodes.rationale: The petal/spoke arrangement of bird bodies radiating outward from a pan centre. This geometry is diagnostic because it is produced by the physical constraint of the circular pan rim rather than by social attraction alone, so counting rosette petals approximates instantaneous feeder occupancy without needing individual identity tracking.

nodes.label: Flock Dispersal and Floor Distribution Pattern
nodes.rationale: How birds spread over the litter floor when not feeding — large drifts against the sides with bare aisles between them. Uneven distribution of this kind is a standard proxy for environmental gradients (temperature, draught, light) inside the house, so the same overhead frames support both behaviour and environment inference.
nodes.norm_label: flock dispersal and floor distribution pattern

nodes.label: Infrared Night-Vision Capture Mode
nodes.rationale: Under dark-period lighting the camera switches to monochrome IR: colour cues vanish, the red feeder caps become indistinguishable from the pan body, contrast between bird and litter drops, and sensor noise rises. Roughly half of this chunk's frames are captured this way, so any model trained on the dataset must handle both appearance regimes.

nodes.label: Colour/Infrared Illumination Domain Shift
nodes.rationale: Deliberately sampling both colour daylight frames and monochrome IR frames of the same scene forces a detector to rely on shape and texture rather than the strong white-bird-on-dark-litter colour contrast. The cost is a harder learning problem; the benefit is round-the-clock inference without a separate night model, which matters because feeding and resting behaviour differ most between light and dark periods.

nodes.label: Burned-In Timestamp and Camera Label Overlay
nodes.rationale: Every frame carries a top-right date-time string and a top-left camera identifier rendered by the DVR into the pixels. This gives free per-frame provenance (which camera, which moment, therefore which bird age and which light period) but also injects fixed high-contrast text that can be learned as a spurious feature or trigger false detections at the image border.
nodes.norm_label: burned-in timestamp and camera label overlay

nodes.label: Camera 1080P-IPC-Siren
nodes.rationale: The dominant camera in this chunk, supplying frames 02101, 02501, 025501, 03201 and 03801 across both colour and infrared modes and across several weeks of the grow-out.

nodes.label: Camera 1080P-IPC-Gas
nodes.rationale: A second camera position, named after the gas brooder zone it overlooks, contributing frame 02701. Its slightly different height and angle change apparent bird scale and feeder spacing, which is why camera identity is worth tracking as metadata rather than pooling all frames as one distribution.

nodes.label: Gas Brooder Heater Canopy
nodes.rationale: The conical radiant heater visible at the top-right of frame02701. Brooders create a warm zone that competes with feeders for bird attention, so their position is a confound when interpreting clustering as feeding rather than thermoregulation.

nodes.label: Litter Floor Substrate
nodes.rationale: The bedding surface the birds stand on, visibly drier and paler in the February frames and darker, wetter and more trodden by mid-March. It is the background class against which white birds are segmented, and its darkening over the cycle steadily changes the foreground/background contrast the model sees.

nodes.label: Broiler Growth-Stage Progression Across the Grow-Out Cycle
nodes.rationale: Timestamps run from 22 February to 14 March 2022 and apparent bird size grows correspondingly, from small scattered chicks to near-market broilers filling the frame. Sampling the whole cycle rather than one day means the detector must cope with object scale changing several-fold under a fixed camera, which is the main reason frames from different dates cannot be treated as interchangeable.
nodes.norm_label: broiler growth-stage progression across the grow-out cycle

nodes.label: Stocking Density and Occlusion Severity
nodes.rationale: By the late frames birds touch and overlap almost everywhere, so individual outlines merge into continuous white mass. This caps the accuracy any per-bird bounding-box detector can reach late in the cycle and argues for density-estimation or region-level occupancy metrics as a complementary readout.

nodes.label: Feeder Occupancy as a Welfare and Health Indicator
nodes.rationale: Contrasting frames where pans are full and ringed with birds against frames where pans are empty and unattended shows why the number of birds at the feed line over time is the target signal: a sustained drop relative to the flock's own baseline flags feed-system failure or disease before it is visible in weight records, and it can be measured from imagery alone without touching the birds.
nodes.norm_label: feeder occupancy as a welfare and health indicator

nodes.label: Frame Sampling for Behaviour-Detection Training Data
nodes.rationale: The img/ directory holds sparsely numbered stills (02101, 02501, 025501, 02701, 03201, 03801) decimated from continuous video. Sampling widely separated frames instead of consecutive ones maximises appearance diversity per annotation hour and avoids the near-duplicate redundancy that inflates apparent accuracy when consecutive video frames leak between train and validation splits.
nodes.norm_label: frame sampling for behaviour-detection training data

nodes.label: Frame 04701 - Daylight Broiler House Overhead (IPC-Gas, 2022-02-23 11:04:26)
nodes.description: Color overhead CCTV still of a commercial broiler house floor. A horizontal suspended feed line runs left-to-right across the mid-frame carrying five white pan feeders with red central cones. Several hundred small white broilers (early growth stage, small body footprint) are densely packed, with a large amorphous aggregation blob in the upper-centre and tight rosettes of birds ringing each feeder pan. Litter floor is visible and bare in the lower third. OSD burn-in: camera name '1080P-IPC-Gas' top-left, timestamp top-right.
nodes.rationale: Serves as a training-split exemplar of the daylight, high-contrast, colour imaging regime with clear bird/litter separation - the easiest condition for a detector and therefore the implicit visual baseline the harder night/IR frames are compared against.

nodes.label: Frame 06701 - Late-Stage Dispersed Flock at Night (IPC-Siren, 2022-03-01 23:05:59)
nodes.description: Colour overhead still captured at 23:05 yet fully colour-exposed, implying house lights were on. Birds are markedly larger than in the February frames (advanced growth stage), individually resolvable, and spread almost uniformly across the whole floor rather than clustered. Many are settled/lying in a resting posture. The five pan feeders are only lightly attended. Litter is visibly darker and more compacted.
nodes.rationale: Demonstrates the late-cycle appearance shift: fewer, larger, more separable birds but near-total floor coverage, which inverts the detection difficulty from occlusion-by-crowding toward whole-frame saturation.
nodes.norm_label: frame 06701 - late-stage dispersed flock at night (ipc-siren, 2022-03-01 23:05:59)

nodes.label: Frame 07101 - Infrared Night Capture, Sparse Flock (IPC-Siren, 2022-02-24 22:06:12)
nodes.description: Monochrome infrared night-vision still - the camera has switched to IR cut-filter-removed mode, so the image is greyscale with washed-out low-saturation tones and the red feeder cones appear as neutral grey. Bird density is the lowest of the six frames; small birds are loosely scattered with visible bare litter between them. Strong barrel/fisheye curvature is evident in the bowed feed line and the arcing dark cable near the bottom edge.
nodes.rationale: Represents the hardest imaging regime in the dataset - low contrast, no colour channel information, and IR glare on the plastic feeders - so bird/litter separation must rely on shape and texture alone.
nodes.norm_label: frame 07101 - infrared night capture, sparse flock (ipc-siren, 2022-02-24 22:06:12)

nodes.label: Test Frame 00097 - Peak-Density Flock (IPC-Siren, 2022-02-26 23:11:16)
nodes.description: Colour overhead still from the held-out test split showing the highest stocking density of the six frames - mid-size broilers blanket the upper two-thirds of the floor with heavy mutual occlusion and touching body outlines. All five pan feeders visibly contain pale feed. A cleared band of bare litter runs across the lower third below the feed line.
nodes.rationale: The crowding here makes instance boundaries ambiguous, which is exactly the regime where counting/detection error concentrates - a deliberate stress case for the evaluation split.

nodes.label: Test Frame 00201 - IR Morning Frame, Feeders Empty and Unattended (IPC-Siren, 2022-02-22 08:53:12)
nodes.description: Greyscale infrared still timestamped 08:53 in the morning yet captured in IR night mode, indicating house lights were still off. The five pan feeders appear empty - the pans read as open lattice with no feed mass inside - and, unusually, almost no birds are positioned at them. The flock has instead drifted into a dense mass in the upper-right quadrant, leaving a wide bare arc around the feed line. Pronounced fisheye barrel distortion bows the feed line and the lower boundary cable.
nodes.rationale: The pairing of empty pans with abandoned feeders is the clearest causal cue in the chunk that feeder occupancy is driven by feed availability rather than by a fixed circadian schedule.
nodes.norm_label: test frame 00201 - ir morning frame, feeders empty and unattended (ipc-siren, 2022-02-22 08:53:12)

nodes.label: Test Frame 00289 - Near-Duplicate of Frame 00097, +12 Seconds (IPC-Siren, 2022-02-26 23:11:28)
nodes.description: Colour overhead still from the same camera, same day and same minute as test frame 00097, exactly twelve seconds later. Scene geometry, lighting, feed level in the pans and litter pattern are essentially identical; only the birds have shifted, having vacated more of the lower-centre floor and compacted further toward the top of the frame. Feed is still visible in all five pans.
nodes.rationale: Nearly all image content is shared with frame 00097, so the two frames are not statistically independent evaluation samples despite carrying different filenames.
nodes.norm_label: test frame 00289 - near-duplicate of frame 00097, +12 seconds (ipc-siren, 2022-02-26 23:11:28)

nodes.label: 1080P-IPC-Gas Camera Viewpoint
nodes.description: One of two named fixed IP-camera installations whose identifier is burned into the top-left OSD as '1080P-IPC-Gas'. It observes a broiler pen with the same five-pan suspended feed-line layout as the Siren camera but from a slightly flatter, less distorted angle.
nodes.rationale: The 'Gas' suffix most plausibly names the environmental stimulus or zone the camera monitors rather than the camera hardware, which would make the camera identifier a proxy for experimental condition.

nodes.label: 1080P-IPC-Siren Camera Viewpoint
nodes.description: The dominant camera installation in this chunk, labelled '1080P-IPC-Siren' in the OSD, contributing five of the six frames and appearing in both the training img/ directory and the held-out img_test/ directory. Its view is more strongly barrel-distorted than the Gas camera and includes a curved dark boundary cable across the lower frame.
nodes.rationale: Because this single camera supplies frames on both sides of the train/test partition, split independence rests on temporal separation alone, not on viewpoint separation.

nodes.label: Suspended Five-Pan Feed Line Rig
nodes.description: The rigid horizontal pipe carrying five evenly spaced circular pan feeders (white lattice pan, red central delivery cone) that crosses every frame at roughly the same height. It is the only geometrically stable, high-contrast structure in the scene across all lighting conditions and both cameras.
nodes.rationale: Its invariance makes it the natural spatial reference for registering frames, defining feeder-proximity zones for behaviour scoring, and estimating the lens distortion field.

nodes.label: Fixed Overhead Surveillance Framing
nodes.description: The shared acquisition geometry of the dataset: a ceiling-mounted static camera looking down at a shallow oblique angle onto the litter floor, producing top-down teardrop-shaped bird silhouettes with minimal side profile and no camera motion between frames.
nodes.rationale: A static overhead rig means background subtraction and fixed region-of-interest masks remain valid across the whole corpus, but it also means birds are only ever seen from one pose family, limiting what a detector can learn about body orientation.

nodes.label: Burned-In Timestamp and Camera-Name OSD Overlay
nodes.description: Every frame carries DVR on-screen-display text rendered directly into the pixel data: the camera identifier in the top-left corner and an ISO-style 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' timestamp in the top-right corner.
nodes.rationale: The overlay supplies free per-frame acquisition metadata that would otherwise be lost when video is decomposed into stills, but because it is pixel-level rather than sidecar metadata it also occupies image area a convolutional model will see and can memorise.
nodes.norm_label: burned-in timestamp and camera-name osd overlay

nodes.label: Feeder-Centric Flock Aggregation
nodes.description: The recurring spatial signature in which birds form tight radial rosettes around each pan feeder, heads inward, producing local density far above the pen average while intervening litter stays comparatively bare.
nodes.rationale: Feeder rings are the highest-information region for welfare inference - occupancy around the pans tracks feeding motivation and competition - but they are also where mutual occlusion is worst, so the most behaviourally meaningful pixels are the hardest ones to segment.

nodes.label: Dispersed Resting Distribution
nodes.description: The contrasting spatial state in which birds are spread near-uniformly over the available floor, largely settled or lying, with no strong attraction to the feeders and low local density variance.
nodes.rationale: Treated as the behavioural counterpoint to feeder aggregation: the ratio of dispersed-resting to feeder-clustered floor area over time is the quantity that makes flock distribution usable as a welfare or disturbance indicator.

nodes.label: Broiler Growth-Stage Progression Across Capture Dates
nodes.description: The systematic increase in per-bird pixel footprint as capture dates advance from 2022-02-22 through 2022-03-01: February frames show small, numerous birds while the March frame shows visibly larger, more separable birds occupying the same physical pen.
nodes.rationale: Apparent object scale is confounded with capture date rather than with camera distance, so a detector trained on early-cycle frames faces a distribution shift at test time and any fixed-size anchor or fixed-radius counting kernel will degrade across the grow-out cycle.
nodes.norm_label: broiler growth-stage progression across capture dates

nodes.label: Infrared Night-Mode Capture Regime
nodes.description: The automatic camera mode in which the IR cut filter is withdrawn under low light, yielding monochrome frames with compressed dynamic range, IR hotspots on plastic surfaces, and no usable colour channel. Two of the six frames in this chunk are in this mode.
nodes.rationale: It splits the corpus into two visually incompatible domains from a single physical camera, meaning colour-dependent cues such as the red feeder cones vanish entirely and any model must either be colour-invariant or be trained on both domains.

nodes.label: Frame Index Does Not Track Chronology
nodes.description: Filename sequence numbers are not monotonic in acquisition time: frame07101 is stamped 2022-02-24 22:06 while the lower-numbered frame06701 is stamped 2022-03-01 23:05, a six-day inversion. Numbering therefore reflects extraction or concatenation order across multiple source recordings, not a single continuous timeline.
nodes.rationale: Any temporal split, tracking pass, or 'hold out the last N frames' strategy that assumes filename order equals time order will silently interleave recording sessions; the burned-in OSD timestamp, not the index, must be treated as the authoritative time key.
nodes.norm_label: frame index does not track chronology

nodes.label: High Stocking Density and Mutual Occlusion
nodes.description: The condition in which birds tile the floor with touching or overlapping silhouettes so that individual instance boundaries are not recoverable from a single frame and the flock reads as continuous white texture rather than as countable objects.
nodes.rationale: This sets the practical ceiling on per-bird detection accuracy and is the main argument for treating the problem as density estimation or region-level behaviour scoring rather than exhaustive individual instance counting.
nodes.norm_label: high stocking density and mutual occlusion

nodes.label: img/ Versus img_test/ Directory Split Convention
nodes.description: The dataset partitions frames by directory rather than by manifest file: img/ holds the training frames and img_test/ holds the evaluation frames, each using an independent frameNNNNN.png numbering series that restarts from zero.
nodes.rationale: Directory-based splitting is simple and tool-agnostic, but here both directories draw on the same camera and overlapping calendar dates, so the partition does not by itself guarantee that train and test frames are independent samples.
nodes.norm_label: img/ versus img_test/ directory split convention

nodes.label: Empty Feeder Pan State
nodes.description: An observable binary scene state in which the pan feeders contain no visible feed mass and read as open lattice, contrasted with the filled state where a pale feed bed fills each pan. In this chunk the empty state co-occurs with an almost total absence of birds at the feed line.
nodes.rationale: Feed presence is directly visible in the same frame as the behaviour it drives, so it can be used as an observed covariate to distinguish genuine appetite or welfare signals from mere feed-delivery scheduling artefacts.

nodes.label: Fisheye Barrel Distortion Field
nodes.description: The wide-angle lens geometry that bows nominally straight structures - the feed line and the floor boundary cable both arc noticeably - and shrinks apparent object size toward the frame periphery relative to the centre.
nodes.rationale: Uncorrected, it makes pixel area a biased estimator of physical floor area, so density, spacing and distribution-uniformity metrics computed in raw image coordinates systematically under-weight the pen edges unless the frames are undistorted first.

nodes.label: Temporal Near-Duplicate Frames Within the Test Split
nodes.description: Distinct test-set filenames that are in fact samples from the same short video window: frames 00097 and 00289 are twelve seconds apart on 2022-02-26 at 23:11, sharing identical lighting, feed level, litter pattern and camera geometry, and differing only in individual bird positions.
nodes.rationale: Sampling stills at a rate faster than the scene decorrelates makes the effective test-set size far smaller than the file count suggests, inflating apparent accuracy and shrinking confidence intervals; frames should be grouped by recording window before evaluation.
nodes.norm_label: temporal near-duplicate frames within the test split

nodes.label: Test Frame 00301 - Siren Camera Infrared Night View of Broiler House
nodes.rationale: Grayscale infrared CCTV still (1920x1080) from an overhead poultry-house camera labelled 1080P-IPC-Siren, timestamped 2022-02-22 08:14:16. Shows roughly 100-150 young broilers on a litter floor, a horizontal suspended feed line crossing the frame with five circular pan feeders, and a dark drinker/cable line arcing across the lower third. Serves as a held-out test image for the chicken behaviour detection pipeline.
nodes.norm_label: test frame 00301 - siren camera infrared night view of broiler house

nodes.label: Camera Channel 1080P-IPC-Siren
nodes.rationale: One of at least three distinct named camera channels burned into the test-set overlays (Siren, PIR, Gas). The Siren channel produces monochrome IR frames of a pen with lighter-coloured litter and smaller birds, giving the dataset a separate visual domain from the other channels.

nodes.label: Infrared / Low-Light Grayscale Capture Mode
nodes.rationale: The Siren frames are fully desaturated with flat IR-style illumination, meaning the model must localise birds from texture and silhouette alone with no colour cue. Including such frames in the test split deliberately checks that the detector does not depend on the white-plumage-against-grey-litter colour contrast available in the daylight/colour channels.

nodes.label: Suspended Pan Feeder Line
nodes.rationale: A rigid horizontal supply pipe carrying five evenly spaced circular pan feeders bisects every Siren frame. It is a fixed scene landmark: constant across frames, it provides an implicit spatial reference for locating feeding zones and can be a source of false positives because its bright radial spokes resemble bird outlines.

nodes.label: Feeding Cluster Behaviour Around Pans
nodes.rationale: Birds form dense radial rosettes with heads pointed inward at each pan, the visual signature of active feeding. This head-in ring arrangement is the behaviour class the analysis pipeline is expected to recognise, and it is the hardest configuration to segment because adjacent birds touch and partially occlude one another.

nodes.label: Flock Dispersion and Spatial Distribution
nodes.rationale: Outside the feeder rosettes the birds are loosely and unevenly scattered, with a sparse empty band across the lower half of the pen. Uniformity of dispersion is a standard welfare/comfort indicator, so per-frame bird positions are the raw signal a downstream density or heat-map analysis would consume.

nodes.label: Wide-Angle / Fisheye Lens Distortion
nodes.rationale: Straight structures such as the feed pipe bow visibly and the pen boundary curves at the frame edges, evidence of a wide-angle security lens. The resulting scale gradient means apparent bird size varies strongly with image position, so a counting model cannot assume a constant object scale across the frame.

nodes.label: img_test Multi-Camera Held-Out Frame Set
nodes.rationale: The img_test directory holds sequentially numbered frameNNNNN.png stills sampled from several CCTV recordings rather than one continuous clip. Mixing camera channels, dates, illumination modes and bird ages in one evaluation folder is a deliberate choice to measure generalisation instead of memorisation of a single scene.

nodes.label: Test Frame 00601 - PIR Camera Colour Night View with Brooder
nodes.rationale: Colour CCTV still from the 1080P-IPC-PIR channel, timestamped 2022-02-27 23:43:19. Several hundred white mid-growth broilers pack the litter floor; two grey feed pipes with red-topped pan feeders cross the frame, a glowing brooder/heater unit sits at the right edge, and a large red drinker appears at lower left.
nodes.norm_label: test frame 00601 - pir camera colour night view with brooder

nodes.label: Camera Channel 1080P-IPC-PIR
nodes.rationale: The PIR channel supplies full-colour frames even at 23:43, implying artificial house lighting rather than IR mode. It contributes the highest-density scenes in the test set and is the only channel whose frames include a visible heat source.

nodes.label: Brooder / Heater Attraction Zone
nodes.rationale: A grey housing with a bright orange glowing element occupies the right edge of every PIR frame. Birds crowd noticeably tighter along its perimeter, so proximity to the heat source is a confounder for any density-based welfare metric: clustering there indicates thermal seeking, not distress.

nodes.label: Resting / Sitting Huddle Behaviour
nodes.rationale: Most birds in the night PIR frames are crouched with legs tucked and bodies pressed together, forming an almost continuous white carpet. Sitting birds present a compact rounded blob with no visible neck or legs, a markedly different appearance signature from the elongated standing/feeding posture, which is why a behaviour classifier needs both postures represented.

nodes.label: High Stocking Density Scene
nodes.rationale: Bird count per frame is an order of magnitude higher than in the Siren frames and litter is barely visible in the upper half. Extreme crowd density is the stress case for detection: individual instances merge into one texture, so NMS thresholds tuned on sparse frames will collapse neighbouring birds into single boxes.

nodes.label: Red-Topped Pan Feeder Unit
nodes.rationale: The colour channels show the same pan feeders as the Siren channel but with saturated red cone tops and white cages. The strong red hue is the single most salient non-bird colour in the scene and acts as a reliable anchor for registering feeder positions in colour frames.

nodes.label: Burned-In Timestamp and Channel Name Overlay
nodes.rationale: Every frame carries a white top-right date-time stamp and a top-left channel label rendered by the DVR. This is the only per-frame provenance available (there is no sidecar metadata), so it is what lets frames be grouped into recording sessions and ordered in time - but it is also fixed high-contrast text that a detector may latch onto as a spurious feature.
nodes.norm_label: burned-in timestamp and channel name overlay

nodes.label: Test Frame 00801 - Siren Camera IR View 28 Seconds After Frame 00301
nodes.rationale: Monochrome 1080P-IPC-Siren frame timestamped 2022-02-22 08:14:44, the same pen and identical camera pose as frame00301 but 28 seconds later. The feed line and five pans are pixel-aligned with frame00301 while the birds have redistributed: the rosettes around the pans are looser and more animals have moved to the upper right corner.
nodes.norm_label: test frame 00801 - siren camera ir view 28 seconds after frame 00301

nodes.label: Near-Duplicate Temporal Frame Pair
nodes.rationale: frame00301 and frame00801 share a static background and differ only in bird placement, so the pair isolates the moving foreground from the fixed scene. Useful for background subtraction or motion-based validation, but it also means the two frames are not statistically independent test samples - scoring them as such inflates apparent accuracy.

nodes.label: Reduced Feeder Crowding Between Frames
nodes.rationale: Compared with frame00301 the pans are surrounded by visibly fewer birds and the litter around them is exposed, showing measurable turnover at the feeding stations within half a minute. Feeder occupancy is therefore a fast-changing time series, which argues for sampling frames densely if feeding-time statistics are the target output.

nodes.label: Cross-Channel Illumination Domain Variation
nodes.rationale: The test folder mixes flat monochrome IR frames (Siren) with brightly lit colour frames (PIR, Gas) of visually different pens. This is an intentional domain shift: a model that generalises must handle both, and grayscale/colour-jitter augmentation during training is effectively mandated by the composition of this evaluation set.

nodes.label: Test Frame 00901 - Gas Camera Overhead View of Mature Broilers
nodes.rationale: Colour still from channel 1080P-IPC-Gas timestamped 2022-03-14 22:24:52. A near top-down view of large, nearly market-weight white broilers filling the whole frame, with a single grey feed pipe and four red-topped pan feeders across the middle. Birds appear much larger in pixels than in the other channels because the camera is closer to the floor and the animals are older.
nodes.norm_label: test frame 00901 - gas camera overhead view of mature broilers

nodes.label: Camera Channel 1080P-IPC-Gas
nodes.rationale: Third named CCTV channel in the test set. Its mounting is lower or more vertical than the Siren and PIR cameras, producing the largest apparent bird size and the least perspective foreshortening of the three.

nodes.label: Mature Broiler Growth Stage
nodes.rationale: Birds here have broad bodies, visible red combs and fully feathered white plumage, versus the small fluffy chicks in the February Siren frames. Body size relative to the fixed feeder pans is the visual proxy for flock age, and it changes the target object scale the detector must cover by roughly a factor of three.

nodes.label: Near Top-Down Overhead Viewpoint
nodes.rationale: The Gas frames look almost straight down, so birds appear as rotation-symmetric ovals with arbitrary heading and no consistent up direction. Axis-aligned bounding boxes are a poor fit for such arbitrarily oriented elongated bodies, and rotation augmentation matters far more here than in the oblique Siren view.

nodes.label: Occlusion and Body-Overlap Detection Challenge
nodes.rationale: Adjacent mature birds overlap so heavily that only partial bodies are visible and boundaries between white plumage regions are nearly invisible. This is the dominant failure mode the test set is built to expose: uniform-coloured, mutually occluding, deformable instances of the same class packed edge to edge.

nodes.label: Broiler Age Progression Across the Recording Period
nodes.rationale: The burned-in dates span 2022-02-22 to 2022-03-14, about three weeks, over which bird body size grows dramatically while the fixed house furniture stays identical. The test set therefore samples a whole grow-out cycle, so evaluation implicitly measures robustness to subject scale drift over time, not just per-image accuracy.
nodes.norm_label: broiler age progression across the recording period

nodes.label: Test Frame 01001 - PIR Camera View 22 Seconds After Frame 00601
nodes.rationale: Colour 1080P-IPC-PIR frame timestamped 2022-02-27 23:43:41, the same pen, brooder and red drinker as frame00601 but framed slightly differently - the feed line sits lower and the scene appears marginally zoomed out, with the same wooden pole and litter marks visible.
nodes.norm_label: test frame 01001 - pir camera view 22 seconds after frame 00601

nodes.label: Subtle Camera Viewpoint Shift Within a Session
nodes.rationale: Frames 00601, 01001 and 01101 come from the same PIR recording minute yet the scene is not pixel-aligned: the feed pipe and brooder shift position between them, indicating slight pan/zoom or camera vibration. Any analysis that assumes a fixed homography across a session (static background subtraction, fixed zone masks) would silently break on this channel. Marked as a reading that is visually clear but whose cause - physical camera movement versus digital re-framing - is uncertain.
nodes.norm_label: subtle camera viewpoint shift within a session

nodes.label: Test Frame 01101 - PIR Camera View 28 Seconds After Frame 00601
nodes.rationale: Colour 1080P-IPC-PIR frame timestamped 2022-02-27 23:43:47, six seconds after frame01001 and nearly identical to it: same brooder glow at right, same red drinker at lower left, same resting carpet of birds with only small local movements near the feeders.
nodes.norm_label: test frame 01101 - pir camera view 28 seconds after frame 00601

nodes.label: Fixed-Interval Frame Sequence Sampling
nodes.rationale: Filenames step by 100 (00601, 00801, 00901, 01001, 01101) while timestamps within a session step by only a few seconds, so the stills were decoded at a regular frame stride from continuous video rather than hand-picked. The consequence is heavy redundancy inside a session and abrupt jumps between sessions, which should be accounted for when reporting per-image evaluation metrics.

nodes.label: Gas-Channel Night Flock Frame (2022-03-14 22:25:08)
nodes.rationale: Top-down fixed CCTV still from a commercial broiler house, overlay '1080P-IPC-Gas' top-left and timestamp '2022-03-14 22:25:08' top-right. Near-grown white broilers cover essentially the whole litter floor; a horizontal suspended feed line with five red-topped pan feeders crosses the mid-frame. Serves as a hard test image for detection/counting: individual birds are heavily overlapping and the feeders are almost fully occluded by birds.

nodes.label: Peak Stocking Density / Full Floor Coverage
nodes.rationale: Late-cycle condition in which grown birds tile the visible floor with almost no exposed litter, so per-bird segmentation boundaries disappear. Density itself becomes the measurable behavioural signal (distribution uniformity) rather than individual tracks.
nodes.norm_label: peak stocking density / full floor coverage

nodes.label: White-on-Grey Occlusion and Low-Contrast Detection Challenge
nodes.rationale: All birds are near-identical white plumage on grey litter and touch or overlap each other, so colour and edge cues are weak. This is why such crowded frames are retained in the img_test set: they stress the detector's ability to separate adjacent instances rather than merely find birds.
nodes.norm_label: white-on-grey occlusion and low-contrast detection challenge

nodes.label: 1080P-IPC-Gas Camera Channel
nodes.rationale: One of two named 1080p IP-camera feeds burned into the overlay ('Gas'). The naming appears to identify the house/pen or the stimulus condition being monitored, giving each frame an implicit source-channel label usable for grouping or stratified evaluation.

nodes.label: Siren-Channel Night Flock Frame (2022-03-14 22:13:07)
nodes.rationale: Overhead colour night frame overlaid '1080P-IPC-Siren' and '2022-03-14 22:13:07'. Six pan feeders hang from the feed line; birds form dense arcs pressed against the feeder pans while patches of bare floor remain between feeders, making feeder-centred aggregation directly visible.

nodes.label: 1080P-IPC-Siren Camera Channel
nodes.rationale: The second named camera feed ('Siren'), which supplies the majority of frames in this chunk across three different dates. Its persistence across dates indicates a fixed-mount viewpoint suitable for background-subtraction and zone-based behaviour metrics.

nodes.label: Feeder-Centred Aggregation Behaviour
nodes.rationale: Birds pack head-inward around each pan feeder while surrounding floor stays comparatively open. This spatial signature is the observable proxy for feeding activity from a single overhead view, since beak-level actions are not resolvable at this scale.

nodes.label: Siren-Channel Flock Frame (2022-03-01 23:00:52)
nodes.rationale: Overhead colour frame, '1080P-IPC-Siren', '2022-03-01 23:00:52'. Mid-size birds are spread fairly evenly with clear litter gaps between them; many are settled or standing still rather than crowding the five visible pan feeders, giving a night resting/idle distribution.

nodes.label: Suspended Pan-Feeder Line
nodes.rationale: A horizontal pipe carrying evenly spaced circular pan feeders with red cone tops crosses every frame at roughly the same height. Because it is static and high-contrast it acts as a natural spatial reference/landmark for registering frames and defining feeder regions of interest.

nodes.label: Dispersed Resting Distribution
nodes.rationale: Even, loosely spaced spread of birds with visible inter-bird litter, contrasting with tight feeder arcs. Provides the negative/baseline class needed to make an aggregation metric meaningful.

nodes.label: Siren-Channel Night Flock Frame (2022-03-14 22:13:13)
nodes.rationale: Overhead colour frame, '1080P-IPC-Siren', '2022-03-14 22:13:13' — six seconds after the other Siren frame of the same date. Same six feeders, same blue equipment at top edge; bird positions have shifted only slightly, so the pair captures short-interval motion.

nodes.label: Six-Second Temporally Adjacent Frame Pair
nodes.rationale: Two test frames from the same camera and date separated by ~6 s show a near-identical scene. Such pairs let displacement/activity be estimated between frames and also reveal near-duplicate leakage risk if test images were sampled from one continuous clip.

nodes.label: Burned-In Timestamp and Channel Overlay
nodes.rationale: Every frame carries a top-right date-time string and a top-left channel name rendered into the pixels. This supplies free per-image metadata (date, hour, camera) for stratifying results, but the bright text is also a fixed artefact that can bias models trained on raw crops.

nodes.label: Siren-Channel Infrared Night Frame (2022-02-24 22:00:59)
nodes.rationale: Monochrome IR night-mode frame, '1080P-IPC-Siren', '2022-02-24 22:00:59'. Smaller younger birds are sparse on the litter and form clean radial rosettes around four pan feeders; a curtain/cable arc and vignetting are visible at the bottom. The cleanest frame for individual-bird detection in this chunk.

nodes.label: Infrared Grayscale Night-Vision Mode
nodes.rationale: The camera switches to single-channel IR when house lights are off, removing the red feeder cones and all colour cues and flattening bird-versus-litter contrast. A model must therefore generalise across colour and grayscale domains within the same nominal camera.

nodes.label: Radial Ring Formation Around Feeder Pans
nodes.rationale: At low stocking density the feeding posture resolves into a distinct spoke/rosette pattern of bodies radiating outward from each pan rim. This geometric template is countable (birds per pan) and is the low-density counterpart of the crowded arcs seen in later frames.
nodes.norm_label: radial ring formation around feeder pans

nodes.label: Gas-Channel Daytime Flock Frame (2022-02-23 11:01:28)
nodes.rationale: Overhead colour daytime frame, '1080P-IPC-Gas', '2022-02-23 11:01:28'. Young pale chicks form loose patches over bare litter around four pan feeders; a brooder/heater hood is partly visible at the right edge, indicating an early rearing stage.

nodes.label: Daytime Colour Imaging Condition
nodes.rationale: The only mid-morning frame in the chunk; ambient light gives full colour, warmer litter tone and softer shadows than the artificially lit night frames. Including it makes the test set span the diurnal illumination range the deployed model will face.

nodes.label: Early Growth-Stage Flock (Small Birds, Low Density)
nodes.rationale: Birds occupy only a fraction of the pixel area of the March frames and leave large bare-litter regions. Apparent object scale therefore varies several-fold across the test set purely from bird age, which is a scale-generalisation requirement for the detector.
nodes.norm_label: early growth-stage flock (small birds, low density)

nodes.label: Flock Growth Progression Across the Production Cycle
nodes.rationale: Ordering the chunk by burned-in date (23 Feb, 24 Feb, 01 Mar, 14 Mar) traces bird size increasing and free floor area shrinking from sparse chicks to a wall-to-wall carpet, i.e. the frames sample one rearing cycle rather than independent scenes.
nodes.norm_label: flock growth progression across the production cycle

nodes.label: Frame 01701 - Infrared Overhead Broiler House View (Siren Camera, 2022-02-22 08:15:34)
nodes.rationale: Grayscale IR ceiling-mounted wide-angle capture of a commercial broiler house. A horizontal suspended feed line crosses the frame with five circular pan feeders; mid-growth birds form dense rosette clusters around each pan while the mid-floor stays comparatively empty. Serves as an unlabelled test-set frame for chicken detection / behaviour analysis.
nodes.norm_label: frame 01701 - infrared overhead broiler house view (siren camera, 2022-02-22 08:15:34)

nodes.label: Frame 02001 - Colour Overhead Broiler House View (Siren Camera, 2022-03-01 23:01:37)
nodes.rationale: Full-colour night capture under artificial house lighting. Birds are near market weight, floor coverage is close to wall-to-wall, and the litter is visibly dark and wet. The hardest frame in the chunk for instance separation because bird silhouettes merge into continuous white mass.
nodes.norm_label: frame 02001 - colour overhead broiler house view (siren camera, 2022-03-01 23:01:37)

nodes.label: Frame 02201 (copy 1) - Colour Overhead View from Gas Camera (2022-02-23 11:02:07)
nodes.rationale: Daytime colour frame from a second, differently labelled camera (1080P-IPC-Gas) covering a different pen. Mid-growth birds, four to five red-topped pan feeders on the feed line, and a red brooder heater hood intruding at the top-right corner.
nodes.norm_label: frame 02201 (copy 1) - colour overhead view from gas camera (2022-02-23 11:02:07)

nodes.label: Frame 02201 - Infrared Overhead Broiler House View (Siren Camera, 2022-02-22 08:55:09)
nodes.rationale: IR grayscale frame captured about forty minutes after frame01701 from the same Siren camera. Birds have partly dispersed away from the feeders toward the upper-left and upper-right of the pen, giving a contrasting spatial distribution for the same scene geometry.
nodes.norm_label: frame 02201 - infrared overhead broiler house view (siren camera, 2022-02-22 08:55:09)

nodes.label: Frame 02601 - Colour Overhead Broiler House View (Siren Camera, 2022-03-01 23:02:10)
nodes.rationale: Captured only 33 seconds after frame02001 from the same camera and the same pen; scene layout, lighting and bird population are essentially identical, so the two frames are near-duplicates in information content.
nodes.norm_label: frame 02601 - colour overhead broiler house view (siren camera, 2022-03-01 23:02:10)

nodes.label: Frame 02901 - Infrared Overhead Broiler House View (Siren Camera, 2022-02-24 22:02:21)
nodes.rationale: Late-evening IR frame with markedly lower apparent occupancy than the other Siren frames: birds sit in loose feeder-centred rosettes with wide empty litter between them, making individual birds cleanly separable.
nodes.norm_label: frame 02901 - infrared overhead broiler house view (siren camera, 2022-02-24 22:02:21)

nodes.label: Overhead Wide-Angle CCTV Viewpoint
nodes.rationale: Every frame in the chunk shares one fixed ceiling-mounted wide-angle (barrel-distorted) camera geometry looking straight down on the litter floor. Birds appear as small top-down blobs with no visible head/tail cue in most cases, so behaviour must be read from position and posture rather than from facial or lateral body features. The barrel distortion also means apparent bird size varies with radial distance from the image centre.

nodes.label: Suspended Pan Feeder Line
nodes.rationale: A single horizontal pipe carrying roughly five circular pan feeders bisects every frame. It is the dominant fixed landmark in the scene and functions as a stable spatial reference for registering frames from the same camera and for defining a feeding zone region of interest.

nodes.label: Feeding Aggregation Around Pan Feeders
nodes.rationale: The most visually salient behaviour in the chunk: birds arrange themselves radially around each pan, heads inward, producing a flower/rosette signature. This pattern is what makes feeding behaviour detectable from an overhead view without any per-bird head annotation - the count of birds within a pan radius is a proxy for feeding activity.

nodes.label: Infrared Night-Vision Capture Mode
nodes.rationale: Three of the six frames (01701, 02201, 02901) are monochrome IR captures with low contrast between bird and litter, vignetting toward the frame edges, and no colour cue to separate the red feeder hardware from the birds. A detector trained only on colour frames would lose the feeder-colour prior in this mode.

nodes.label: Burned-In Timestamp and Camera Label Overlay
nodes.rationale: Each frame carries a top-right date-time stamp and a top-left camera name ('1080P-IPC-Siren' / '1080P-IPC-Gas') burned into the pixels. This is free metadata that recovers capture date, time of day and camera identity for frames whose filenames only encode a frame index, but it is also a fixed high-contrast artefact that can bias a detector or a background model if not cropped or masked.
nodes.norm_label: burned-in timestamp and camera label overlay

nodes.label: High Stocking Density Late-Cycle Flock
nodes.rationale: In the 2022-03-01 frames the birds are near market weight and cover nearly the whole floor, so per-bird spacing approaches zero. Density is simultaneously the welfare metric of interest and the main driver of annotation and detection difficulty.

nodes.label: Colour Artificial-Light Capture Mode
nodes.rationale: Frames 02001, 02601 and 02201 (1) are captured in colour. White plumage against grey-brown litter gives strong luminance separation and the red feeder cones become an unambiguous landmark cue - a signal completely unavailable in the IR frames.

nodes.label: Wet / Caked Litter Substrate
nodes.rationale: The 2022-03-01 frames show dark, glossy, compacted litter compared with the dry pale bedding of the February frames. Litter condition is itself a welfare indicator (footpad dermatitis risk) and it also shifts the background appearance distribution, which matters for any background-subtraction or colour-threshold step.

nodes.label: Bird Occlusion and Overlap Detection Challenge
nodes.rationale: At market weight the birds physically touch and overlap, so bounding boxes have very high mutual IoU and non-maximum suppression will merge or drop true positives. This is the concrete reason a test set needs both sparse (frame02901) and saturated (frame02001, frame02601) frames: the sparse ones verify basic localisation, the saturated ones stress crowd separation.
nodes.norm_label: bird occlusion and overlap detection challenge

nodes.label: Gas Camera Viewpoint (1080P-IPC-Gas)
nodes.rationale: A second camera installation labelled 'Gas', covering a different pen with slightly different mounting height and feeder spacing than the 'Siren' camera. Only one frame in this chunk comes from it, so the chunk is heavily Siren-biased.

nodes.label: Brooder Heater Hood
nodes.rationale: A large red conical heater canopy intrudes into the top-right corner of the Gas frame. It is a fixed piece of house infrastructure that shares the red colour signature of the feeder cones, so a naive colour-based feeder locator would produce a false landmark here.

nodes.label: Multi-Camera Poultry House Dataset (Siren and Gas)
nodes.rationale: The burned-in camera labels reveal that the img_test folder mixes at least two distinct camera installations. Frames from different cameras cannot share a hand-drawn region-of-interest mask or a fixed feeder coordinate list, so any spatial prior must be derived per camera.
nodes.norm_label: multi-camera poultry house dataset (siren and gas)

nodes.label: Siren Camera Viewpoint (1080P-IPC-Siren)
nodes.rationale: Five of the six frames in this chunk carry the 'Siren' camera label and share an identical feed-line position and lens distortion, which makes them directly comparable across dates and lighting modes.

nodes.label: Duplicate Frame Filename Collision (frame02201 vs frame02201 (1))
nodes.rationale: Two files share the frame index 02201 but show different cameras, dates and lighting modes (Siren IR 2022-02-22 08:55:09 vs Gas colour 2022-02-23 11:02:07). The ' (1)' suffix is a filesystem copy artefact, which means the frame index alone does not uniquely identify a capture and any index-keyed label file risks being attached to the wrong image. Flagged AMBIGUOUS: whether this is deliberate curation or an accidental duplicate cannot be determined from the images alone.
nodes.norm_label: duplicate frame filename collision (frame02201 vs frame02201 (1))

nodes.label: Near-Consecutive Frame Pair (33 s Apart)
nodes.rationale: frame02001 (23:01:37) and frame02601 (23:02:10) are 33 seconds apart on the same camera, so they are statistically near-duplicates. Keeping both in a test set inflates apparent sample size without adding scene diversity and can leak between train and test if the split is random rather than time-blocked.

nodes.label: Resting / Sitting Posture Cluster
nodes.rationale: Away from the feeders, birds appear as compact rounded blobs with no visible leg or neck extension, consistent with sitting or resting rather than walking or feeding. Posture compactness read from an overhead silhouette is the main cue available for separating resting from active behaviour in this dataset.

nodes.label: Flock Growth Progression Across Capture Dates
nodes.rationale: Apparent bird size grows steadily from the 2022-02-22 frames through 2022-02-23 and 2022-02-24 to the 2022-03-01 frames, spanning roughly a week of the grow-out cycle. Object scale is therefore not stationary across the folder, so a detector with a fixed anchor scale or a fixed-radius counting kernel will degrade at one end of the date range.
nodes.norm_label: flock growth progression across capture dates

nodes.label: Day/Night Domain Gap in Capture Conditions
nodes.rationale: The chunk splits into two visually incompatible domains - monochrome low-contrast IR and full-colour lit frames - captured by the same camera at different hours. This is why the test set deliberately mixes both: a model validated only on colour frames would not be shown to generalise to the IR night regime, which is exactly when much resting behaviour occurs.
nodes.norm_label: day/night domain gap in capture conditions

nodes.label: Frame 03901 - Overhead Broiler House CCTV, Siren Camera, 2022-03-01 23:03:23
nodes.description: Top-down colour CCTV still of a commercial broiler house floor, camera label '1080P-IPC-Siren', burned-in timestamp 2022-03-01 23:03:23. Near-market-weight white broilers densely cover the litter floor. A horizontal grey feed conveyor pipe crosses the frame carrying five red-topped circular pan feeders; birds form radial rosettes around each pan. A dark winch/tension cable arcs across the lower third. Barrel distortion from a wide-angle lens is visible.
nodes.norm_label: frame 03901 - overhead broiler house cctv, siren camera, 2022-03-01 23:03:23

nodes.label: Frame 04101 - Overhead Broiler House CCTV, Siren Camera, 2022-03-01 23:03:34
nodes.description: Same Siren-camera viewpoint 11 seconds after frame 03901. Identical feed line and five pan feeders; birds have shifted slightly, floor patches are marginally more exposed. Useful as a near-duplicate temporal pair for motion/behaviour-change analysis.
nodes.norm_label: frame 04101 - overhead broiler house cctv, siren camera, 2022-03-01 23:03:34

nodes.label: Frame 04901 - Infrared Night-Vision Broiler House CCTV, Siren Camera, 2022-02-24 22:04:11
nodes.description: Monochrome infrared night-vision still from the Siren camera, timestamp 2022-02-24 22:04:11. Birds are noticeably smaller (earlier in the grow-out cycle) and far more dispersed than in the March colour frames. Same feed pipe and pan feeders, rendered without the red feeder caps because of the IR/greyscale sensor mode.
nodes.norm_label: frame 04901 - infrared night-vision broiler house cctv, siren camera, 2022-02-24 22:04:11

nodes.label: Frame 05101 - Overhead Broiler House CCTV, Siren Camera, 2022-03-01 23:04:29
nodes.description: Colour Siren-camera still one minute after frame 04101. Very high stocking density with heavy inter-bird occlusion and overlapping body outlines; feeder rosettes are less distinct because the surrounding flock is continuous. Represents the hardest detection/counting case in this chunk.
nodes.norm_label: frame 05101 - overhead broiler house cctv, siren camera, 2022-03-01 23:04:29

nodes.label: Frame 05401 - Overhead Broiler House CCTV, Gas Camera, 2022-02-23 11:05:06
nodes.description: Colour daytime still from a different camera, label '1080P-IPC-Gas', timestamp 2022-02-23 11:05:06. Young/small broilers on largely bare litter; four pan feeders on the feed pipe plus a red brooder/heater cone at upper right. Birds form a large loose clump above the feed line and tight rosettes at each pan, with much exposed floor elsewhere.
nodes.norm_label: frame 05401 - overhead broiler house cctv, gas camera, 2022-02-23 11:05:06

nodes.label: Frame 05601 - Infrared Night-Vision Broiler House CCTV, Siren Camera, 2022-02-24 22:04:49
nodes.description: Monochrome IR night-vision still from the Siren camera 38 seconds after frame 04901. Same dispersed early-cycle flock, feed pipe and pan feeders; birds are mostly stationary or lightly feeding, with wide areas of open litter.
nodes.norm_label: frame 05601 - infrared night-vision broiler house cctv, siren camera, 2022-02-24 22:04:49

nodes.label: Siren Camera Viewpoint (1080P-IPC-Siren)
nodes.description: Named fixed overhead IP camera whose watermark '1080P-IPC-Siren' appears on frames 03901, 04101, 04901, 05101 and 05601. Defines one recording station/pen in the broiler house.
nodes.rationale: A per-camera watermark plus burned-in timestamp lets frames be grouped back into recording sessions and pens after they have been flattened into a single img_test folder, which is why the overlay is retained rather than cropped out.

nodes.label: Gas Camera Viewpoint (1080P-IPC-Gas)
nodes.description: Second named fixed overhead IP camera, watermark '1080P-IPC-Gas', source of frame 05401. Covers a different pen/zone with a visible brooder heater cone and younger birds.

nodes.label: Suspended Pan Feeder Line
nodes.description: Horizontal feed conveyor pipe carrying evenly spaced circular pan feeders with red control caps, running across every frame in this chunk. The dominant fixed landmark of the scene.
nodes.rationale: Because the feeder line is static across all frames and cameras, it acts as a natural spatial reference/anchor for registering frames and for defining a feeding zone region-of-interest.

nodes.label: Feeding Cluster (Radial Rosette at Pan Feeder)
nodes.description: Recurrent behavioural pattern in which birds arrange themselves head-in around a pan feeder, producing a radial rosette/flower shape from overhead. Visible at every pan in frames 03901, 04101, 05101, 05401 and weakly in the IR night frames.
nodes.rationale: The rosette is the visual signature the analysis pipeline can key on to score feeding activity without individual tracking - counting birds inside a feeder radius is far more robust than classifying posture in a top-down, heavily occluded view.
nodes.norm_label: feeding cluster (radial rosette at pan feeder)

nodes.label: Flock Density and Floor Distribution
nodes.description: Spatial spread of birds over the litter floor, ranging from near-total floor coverage in the March colour frames to sparse dispersion in the February IR frames. A core welfare/behaviour metric derivable from overhead stills.

nodes.label: Infrared Night-Vision Capture Mode
nodes.description: Greyscale IR imaging mode the cameras switch into after dark (frames 04901 and 05601, both ~22:04). Removes colour cues such as the red feeder caps and lowers contrast between birds and litter.
nodes.rationale: Any detector trained on these frames must be colour-invariant, since the same scene appears in both RGB and monochrome IR depending on time of day - which is why both modalities are represented in the held-out img_test set.

nodes.label: Nocturnal Resting / Low-Activity State
nodes.description: Night-time behavioural state inferred from the IR frames: birds are widely spread, largely stationary, and only lightly attending the feeders, in contrast to the compact feeder-centred crowding of the lit frames.
nodes.rationale: Comparing dispersion at the same clock hour across the flock cycle is a cheap proxy for disturbance/stress, so night frames are deliberately kept in the test set rather than discarded as low-quality.

nodes.label: Burned-In Timestamp and Camera Label Overlay
nodes.description: DVR overlay printing the camera name at top-left and 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' at top-right of every frame. Supplies the only per-frame temporal and source metadata, since filenames carry just a sequence number.
nodes.norm_label: burned-in timestamp and camera label overlay

nodes.label: Broiler Growth-Stage Variation Across Capture Dates
nodes.description: Apparent bird size increases markedly from 2022-02-23 and 2022-02-24 (small, well-separated birds, much bare litter) to 2022-03-01 (large birds covering the floor), reflecting broiler grow-out over roughly one week.
nodes.rationale: Sampling frames across grow-out dates makes the evaluation set cover a wide object-scale range, so a model cannot succeed by assuming a single bird size in pixels.
nodes.norm_label: broiler growth-stage variation across capture dates

nodes.label: Overhead Wide-Angle (Fisheye-Distorted) Viewpoint
nodes.description: All frames are ceiling-mounted top-down views with visible barrel distortion - straight structures such as the feed pipe and floor cable bow across the frame, and birds near the edges are foreshortened.

nodes.label: Off-Feeder Huddling Clump
nodes.description: Large loose aggregation of young birds away from the pan feeders in frame 05401, near the brooder heater cone rather than around feed.
nodes.rationale: Distinguishing a thermally driven huddle from a feeding rosette matters for welfare scoring: identical local density means opposite things depending on whether the cluster centre is a feeder or a heat source.

nodes.label: img_test Held-Out Evaluation Frame Set
nodes.description: The img_test directory these frames belong to: sparsely sampled stills (frame03901, 04101, 04901, 05101, 05401, 05601 - roughly every 200-800 frames) drawn from multiple cameras, dates, lighting modes and bird ages.
nodes.rationale: Wide stride between sampled frame numbers avoids near-duplicate leakage between train and test, while deliberately mixing cameras, day/night and growth stages keeps the evaluation set representative of deployment conditions.

nodes.label: Dense Mutual Occlusion Challenge
nodes.description: At peak stocking density birds overlap and merge into continuous white regions with no separating background, so individual outlines are ambiguous even to a human annotator.
nodes.rationale: This is the principal failure mode for bounding-box detection and counting in this dataset, and motivates density-estimation or feeder-zone-aggregate metrics as fallbacks to per-bird detection.

nodes.label: Overhead Broiler House CCTV Frame 05701
nodes.description: Raw, unannotated top-down surveillance still extracted from commercial broiler-house video. Shows several hundred white broiler chickens densely packed on a litter/dirt floor, a horizontal suspended feed pipe carrying five red-and-white circular pan feeders across the middle of the frame, and a dark drinker/nipple line curving across the lower third. Burnt-in overlays: '1080P-IPC-Siren' (camera/stream identity, top-left) and '2022-03-01 23:05:03' (top-right). This is pipeline input data, not model output — the img_test directory supplies real deployment frames for chicken detection and behavior analysis.
nodes.rationale: A fixed ceiling-mounted camera was chosen over ground-level cameras because it yields near-constant scale and unobstructed coverage of the whole pen, which is what makes per-bird counting and spatial (feeder-proximity) behavior scoring tractable.

nodes.label: Dense Flock Occlusion and Small-Object Regime
nodes.description: The visual regime the detector must survive: hundreds of near-identical white birds at low pixel-area each, heavily overlapping and touching, against a low-contrast grey litter background, with birds partially hidden under feeder pans and behind the feed pipe. Individuals are separable mainly by body-axis orientation and shadow gaps rather than by colour or texture.
nodes.rationale: This is the hardest case for both the detector (small, low-contrast, class-uniform objects) and the tracker (identity switches when boxes overlap), and it explains why a dedicated fine-tuned model is needed rather than off-the-shelf COCO weights.
nodes.norm_label: dense flock occlusion and small-object regime

nodes.label: Suspended Pan Feeder and Drinker Line as Spatial Landmarks
nodes.description: Fixed house infrastructure visible in every frame: five circular pan feeders on a rigid horizontal pipe, plus a drinker line lower in the frame. Birds visibly cluster in rosettes around each pan. Because the camera is static, these structures occupy constant image coordinates and can serve as reference regions.
nodes.rationale: Feeder and drinker positions are stable across the whole recording, so feeding/drinking behavior can be scored geometrically (bird centroid inside or near a feeder region) instead of requiring a separate learned behavior classifier.
nodes.norm_label: suspended pan feeder and drinker line as spatial landmarks

nodes.label: Burnt-in Camera ID and Timestamp Overlay
nodes.description: Non-removable pixel overlay rendered by the IP camera itself: stream label '1080P-IPC-Siren' and wall-clock timestamp '2022-03-01 23:05:03'. It anchors each extracted frame to absolute time (here a night-time recording under artificial light), enabling diurnal behavior analysis, but it also injects high-contrast text into the image that a detector may hallucinate on.
nodes.rationale: Keeping the burnt-in timestamp trades a small risk of spurious detections in the overlay corners for the ability to align frame indices with real clock time without a separate metadata sidecar.
nodes.norm_label: burnt-in camera id and timestamp overlay

nodes.label: Fixed Top-Down Viewpoint
nodes.description: The nadir/near-nadir camera geometry of the target domain: no perspective foreshortening between foreground and background, negligible scale variation across the frame, no horizon, and object appearance dominated by rotation in the image plane. Contrasts sharply with the ground-level, strong-perspective viewpoint of the bundled tracker and detector demo assets.
nodes.rationale: Constant object scale removes the need for heavy multi-scale reasoning but makes rotation invariance the dominant requirement, so demo assets shot from ground level are a poor proxy for expected accuracy on this domain.

nodes.label: Cars Multi-Object Tracking Demo GIF
nodes.description: Animated 480x270, 111-frame result clip advertising the multi-object-tracker library. A ground-level camera beside a racetrack guardrail watches a line of classic convertibles drive past. Every vehicle carries a thin blue axis-aligned bounding box with a small cyan track-label above it and green centroid/keypoint dots inside. Identity boxes persist and shrink smoothly as cars recede up the track, demonstrating tracking continuity rather than per-frame detection quality.
nodes.rationale: Vehicles on a track were chosen for the headline demo because they move fast and monotonically with little mutual occlusion, which showcases the motion model cleanly.

nodes.label: Persistent Track ID Box Overlay Convention
nodes.description: The library's standard visual output contract: for each tracked object draw a coloured rectangle, print a compact identifier label at the top-left corner of that rectangle, and mark the tracked point(s) inside. The same box colour and identifier follow an object across frames, so an identity switch is visible to the eye as a colour/label change.
nodes.rationale: Rendering identity as a stable label rather than only a box is what turns a detector visualisation into a tracker visualisation — it is the only way a viewer can verify association quality from a GIF.
nodes.norm_label: persistent track id box overlay convention

nodes.label: Cows Multi-Object Tracking Demo GIF
nodes.description: Animated 480x270, 77-frame tracker result on a coastal beach scene: a small herd of black and brown cattle, some standing and some lying on the sand, beneath chalk cliffs and a cluster of white houses. Tracked animals carry lime-green bounding boxes with small ID labels and green centroid dots. Notably, several background cattle at the left remain untracked, so the clip also illustrates recall failure on distant/low-contrast animals.
nodes.rationale: Cattle are the demo closest to the chicken domain — deformable, same-coloured, partly stationary animals — and the visible misses on small background animals foreshadow exactly the recall problem a dense flock creates.

nodes.label: Livestock Tracking Use Case
nodes.description: Applying generic multi-object tracking to farm animals rather than vehicles or pedestrians: subjects are non-rigid, frequently stationary or lying down, visually near-identical to one another, and appear in unstructured outdoor or barn environments. Standing vs. lying posture is directly readable from box aspect ratio in this clip.
nodes.rationale: This is the demo that justifies adopting this tracker for a poultry project at all — it is evidence the association logic degrades gracefully on animals whose appearance features are weak and whose motion is intermittent.

nodes.label: Centroid Marker as Trajectory Anchor
nodes.description: Each tracked animal is reduced to a single green point drawn at the box centre; that point, not the full box, is the quantity carried forward by the motion model and logged as the object's per-frame position. Trajectories, speed and dwell-time statistics are all derived from this reduced representation.
nodes.rationale: Collapsing a deformable animal to one centroid keeps the state vector small and robust to box jitter caused by posture change, at the cost of losing size/orientation information that a behavior classifier might want.

nodes.label: YOLOv4 Prediction Showcase Figure
nodes.description: README showcase figure for the yolo-v4-tf.keras port: a matplotlib render (visible pixel axes running to ~2050 x ~1500) of inference on a crowded indoor social gathering. A dozen-plus multi-coloured boxes labelled 'person' carry scores from 0.99 down to 0.38, alongside non-person detections 'cake 0.62', 'bottle 0.9x' and 'diningtable'. Boxes overlap heavily and several people at the rear are missed or double-boxed.
nodes.rationale: Publishing a figure that includes low-confidence 0.38 boxes and visible misses, rather than a cherry-picked clean scene, documents the honest operating point of the ported weights.

nodes.label: Class-Plus-Confidence Label Annotation
nodes.description: The detector's drawing convention: every surviving box is captioned with its predicted class name and a two-decimal objectness/class score, with box colour varying per instance. The spread of printed scores (0.99, 0.94, 0.90, 0.84, 0.62, 0.57, 0.40, 0.38) makes the effective score threshold and the NMS behaviour directly auditable from the figure.
nodes.rationale: Printing the numeric score next to each box lets a reader choose a deployment threshold by eye instead of re-running inference, which is why the demo keeps sub-0.5 boxes visible.

nodes.label: COCO Pretrained Multi-Class Detection Baseline
nodes.description: Evidence that the Keras/TensorFlow re-implementation loads and correctly reproduces original Darknet COCO weights, since it emits the standard 80-class vocabulary (person, cake, bottle, diningtable) with plausible scores on an unseen photograph. It is a weight-porting correctness check, not a poultry model.
nodes.rationale: Verifying the port against stock COCO weights before any fine-tuning isolates conversion bugs from training bugs; 'bird' exists in COCO but is not fit for broilers, so domain fine-tuning is still required.

nodes.label: Street Scene Smoke-Test Image
nodes.description: Small, low-resolution (roughly thumbnail-scale) unannotated JPEG of a suburban residential street: a curving road with painted markings, street lamps, hedges and houses, a tall grey tower block on the skyline, and a group of roughly eight adults and children standing on the pavement. Bundled purely as detector input, with no boxes drawn.
nodes.rationale: A deliberately small, mundane, multi-scale street photo is a cheap smoke test — it exercises person detection at several distances without needing a large asset in the repository.

nodes.label: Taiwan AI Academy Award Group Photo Test Image
nodes.description: Wide (~2048x878) unannotated stage photograph used as the default inference input. About twenty-two people in a single row on an auditorium stage in front of a projection screen and beige curtain, most wearing yellow conference lanyards and badges. Two central figures hold a presentation board reading '佳作獎' (Honorable Mention Award) issued by 台灣人工智慧學校 (Taiwan AI Academy), captioned as a first-cohort technical leadership training programme project.
nodes.rationale: Reusing the author's own award photo as the shipped test image both avoids licensing concerns and provides a genuinely hard many-instance case.
nodes.norm_label: taiwan ai academy award group photo test image

nodes.label: Crowded Shoulder-to-Shoulder Instance Benchmark
nodes.description: The stress case this image encodes: ~22 same-class instances standing shoulder-to-shoulder in one horizontal band, mutually occluding at the torso, at nearly identical scale, in a very wide aspect ratio that must be letterboxed into a square network input. Success is measured by instance count and by whether non-maximum suppression merges adjacent people.
nodes.rationale: Many same-class, mutually occluding, uniform-scale instances in one band is structurally the same failure mode as a packed poultry pen, which is why this asset is a meaningful proxy despite the subject matter differing.

nodes.label: Crowded Pedestrian Crossing Test Image
nodes.description: Elevated/oblique photograph of a very busy urban scissor crossing (Shibuya-style) with roughly 60-80 pedestrians walking in multiple directions across white zebra stripes; many wear face masks and carry bags or umbrellas. Used as an unlabelled qualitative test input for the YOLOv4 Keras detector: it exercises the 'person' class at high instance density, heavy mutual occlusion, small object scale and a strongly patterned high-contrast background.

nodes.label: Dense Small-Object Detection Under Occlusion
nodes.rationale: A crowd image is chosen as a smoke test because the hardest failure modes of a one-stage anchor-based detector show up here: NMS merging adjacent same-class boxes, small-scale instances falling below the stride of the coarse detection head, and repetitive stripe texture producing background false positives. If the detector holds up on a dense human crowd it is plausible it will hold up on a dense flock, which is the actual target domain of the project.

nodes.label: Studio Portrait Test Image
nodes.description: Studio press-style headshot: a single smiling woman with shoulder-length hair in a black sleeveless top, centred against a plain white seamless background. The antithesis of test2.jpg - one large, unoccluded, well-lit subject on a clutter-free background.

nodes.label: Single-Subject Detection Baseline
nodes.rationale: Kept as the easy end of the test suite: a near-guaranteed single high-confidence 'person' box. Its purpose is diagnostic separation - if this image fails, the fault is in weight loading, preprocessing or class decoding rather than in detection difficulty, so it isolates pipeline bugs from model-capacity limits.

nodes.label: Indoor Group Gathering Test Image
nodes.description: Candid indoor photo inside a Japanese restaurant / izakaya: about twenty people, mostly a lab or office group, clapping while a woman hands a decorated cake to a man in a green polo. Visible secondary objects include dining tables, bowls, chopsticks, drinking glasses, a cake, a wristwatch, chairs and a wall poster. A mid-density, multi-class, mixed-scale indoor scene under warm artificial light.

nodes.label: Multi-Class Cluttered Indoor Scene Detection
nodes.rationale: Exercises the breadth of the COCO class vocabulary rather than just 'person': cake, dining table, bowl, cup, chair and clock-like objects co-occur at very different scales in one frame. This confirms the pretrained head decodes the full 80-class output correctly before the model is repurposed for the single-class poultry problem.

nodes.label: Vehicle Multi-Object Tracking Demo (cars.gif)
nodes.description: 111-frame 480x270 animated result GIF used as the README demo for the multi-object-tracker package. Classic convertibles drive along a racetrack past a crash barrier; each vehicle carries a blue axis-aligned bounding box with a small green text label (class + numeric track ID) and a green centroid marker. Boxes follow individual cars as they approach, grow in scale and exit the frame, and distant cars near the horizon are also boxed.

nodes.label: Track Identity Persistence Across Frames
nodes.rationale: The GIF is the visual proof that tracking adds something detection alone cannot: a stable integer identity attached to each object across time. Per-frame detection would relabel each car every frame; the persistent ID is what makes downstream per-individual statistics (dwell time, trajectory, behaviour duration) possible at all. This is exactly the property the chicken-behaviour pipeline needs to attribute a behaviour episode to one bird.

nodes.label: Livestock (Cattle) Multi-Object Tracking Demo (cows.gif)
nodes.description: 77-frame 480x270 animated result GIF: a small herd of black and brown cattle on a coastal beach with cliffs and a village in the background. Each animal is enclosed in a green bounding box with a small class/ID caption and a green centroid dot; both standing and lying-down animals are tracked, including strongly overlapping and partially cropped individuals at the frame edge.

nodes.label: Animal Tracking Domain Transfer
nodes.rationale: Retaining the cattle demo alongside the vehicle demo signals that the same centroid/IOU/Kalman association machinery transfers from rigid vehicles to deformable livestock. Animals break the constant-velocity, constant-appearance assumptions that vehicle tracking relies on - they change posture (standing vs lying), stop for long periods and overlap heavily - which is the closest available public analogue to a barn full of chickens.

nodes.label: Edge AI Vision Pipeline Architecture Diagram
nodes.description: Three-column block architecture diagram of a smart poultry-farm system, drawn with dashed swimlane boundaries labelled 'Edge Subsystem', 'Digital Farming Platform' and 'Portals'. Bidirectional arrows carry link-technology annotations (BLE / Lora / Ethernet, Ethernet, 4G). Two blue-shaded blocks with numbered navy callout badges (1 and 2) highlight the contributions of the work: the smart IoT camera nodes at the edge, and the dead-chicken-detection plus chicken-weight-estimation services on the platform.
nodes.norm_label: edge ai vision pipeline architecture diagram

nodes.label: Edge Subsystem
nodes.description: Leftmost dashed swimlane: everything physically inside the poultry house. Contains the sensor IoT nodes, the smart IoT camera nodes and the IoT edge gateway that aggregates them.

nodes.label: IoT Nodes with Sensors
nodes.description: Vertical stack of in-house sensing modalities: microphone, air temperature, air humidity, CO2 level, NH3 (ammonia) level and light. These are the non-visual environmental channels that complement the camera stream.

nodes.label: IoT Edge Gateway
nodes.description: On-farm router/gateway appliance. Speaks BLE, Lora and Ethernet down to the sensor nodes, Ethernet to the camera nodes, and 4G upstream to the cloud platform.
nodes.rationale: A single aggregation point lets the farm expose one managed uplink instead of many, and lets short-range low-power radios (BLE/Lora) be used for battery-powered sensors while the bandwidth-hungry camera nodes stay on wired Ethernet.

nodes.label: Smart IoT Camera Nodes
nodes.description: Blue-shaded block carrying callout badge 1 - the first highlighted contribution. Each node pairs a camera with a co-located edge device, so vision capture and vision inference sit in the same physical unit inside the house.

nodes.label: Edge Device (AI / Inference)
nodes.description: Accelerator/SoC drawn beside each camera, running the detection and estimation models locally.
nodes.rationale: Inference is placed at the edge rather than in the cloud because the uplink is 4G: continuously streaming raw video from every camera is infeasible on cost and bandwidth, and it also raises latency for time-critical alerts. Running the model on-node means only compact structured results (counts, boxes, weights, incident flags) traverse the link, which additionally limits how much raw imagery leaves the farm.

nodes.label: 4G Backhaul Link
nodes.description: Bidirectional 4G arrow between the IoT edge gateway and the cloud IoT platform - the single constrained WAN hop of the whole architecture.
nodes.rationale: Cellular backhaul is chosen because poultry houses are typically rural with no reliable fixed line; its limited and metered bandwidth is the constraint that forces the edge-inference design decision.

nodes.label: Digital Farming Platform
nodes.description: Central dashed swimlane hosting the cloud side: the IoT platform, the farm management service suite, the data storage tier and the portal/API application logic.

nodes.label: IoT Platform
nodes.description: Cloud-side ingestion column with four stacked capabilities: Gateway, Sensor Data, IoT Node Configurations and Security. It terminates the 4G link and mediates between devices and business services.

nodes.label: Sensor Data
nodes.description: Time-series telemetry repository inside the IoT platform holding the readings pushed up from the sensor IoT nodes.

nodes.label: IoT Node Configurations
nodes.description: Device configuration/registry store, giving the downstream (cloud to device) direction of the bidirectional 4G arrow its purpose: remote provisioning and reconfiguration of edge nodes.

nodes.label: Farm Management Service Suite
nodes.description: Central grid of ten business capabilities drawn as blue 'service' glyphs: incident detection, reporting, service book, admin, alert hub, map configuration, integration, environment monitoring, acoustic stress detection and food mix optimization - plus the two blue-shaded contributed services in the callout-2 block below it.

nodes.label: Incident Detection
nodes.description: Farm-management service that turns incoming sensor and vision events into flagged incidents requiring attention.

nodes.label: Alert Hub
nodes.description: Central notification fan-out service that routes detected incidents to the human-facing portals and mobile app.

nodes.label: Environment Monitoring
nodes.description: Service that tracks the in-house climate channels (temperature, humidity, CO2, NH3, light) against acceptable welfare ranges.

nodes.label: Stress Detection (Acoustic)
nodes.description: Service that infers flock stress from vocalisation audio captured by the microphone sensor node - the non-visual counterpart to the camera-based welfare services.
nodes.rationale: Audio is used alongside vision because sound propagates through the whole house and is not blocked by occlusion or poor lighting, so it covers birds the cameras cannot see.

nodes.label: Detection of Dead Chickens
nodes.description: One of the two blue-shaded services in the callout-2 block: computer-vision identification of mortality in the flock.
